She fears that rejecting an expectation will hurt Wei Jian, though he is less demanding about reputation than she assumes. Xu Qing knows some doubts. Their friendship has yet to become anything more. Training choices and private conversations can reveal the tension.
characters.appearance: Athletic young adult woman with a high black ponytail and sharp dark eyes; controlled posture without an unearned aura. Bone-white split practice robes with pine-green panels and close dark bindings at wrist and waist. Pine-green panels open over bone-white silk as she moves; close wrist bindings and a high, swinging ponytail give her silhouette the clarity of a drawn blade. She stands with her sword vertical beside her leg, fingers relaxed around its hilt and her other hand on the scabbard.
traits: Quirk: She is disciplined, proud and privately uncertain about which expectations she wants.
Wants / Fears: She wants to develop a sword art she can honestly call her own and choose the life around it.
Pattern: She speaks in direct complete sentences, restrained courtesy and occasional sharp humour with Xu Qing.

Bond: Wei Jian’s place as her grandfather cannot be separated from his exacting instruction. She continues to see Xu Qing despite the rivalry, keeping a friendship neither institution has managed to extinguish.
abilities: Green Ridge Counter — a measured Foundation Establishment countercut needing an opening.
Held Distance — footwork and qi control preserve useful reach within her capacity.

characters.name: Shen Qiulan
characters.summary: Shen Qiulan’s pride in Verdant Pill Sect begins with the people who walk out of its medicine halls alive.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Shen Qiulan’s pride in Verdant Pill Sect begins with the people who walk out of its medicine halls alive. She has inherited both a formidable alchemical tradition and a confidence in its old safeguards that years of success have made difficult to question. Personally asks patients practical questions before discussing reputation or cultivation. She trusts Hu Song with the cauldron’s custody and respects Jiang Lan’s practical gifts as a physician. The two offer different assurances in a sect whose greatest treasure demands more caution than admiration.
Shen Qiulan learned early that an impressive furnace result could conceal a patient’s later decline. She asks for accounts of recovery as well as the announced yield and keeps time in her day for ordinary consultations that a sect mistress could easily delegate. Her garden walks are partly inspection and partly the only interval in which nobody immediately places a decision before her. She enjoys the smell of properly prepared food more than costly incense and can be quietly irritated when a formal meal arrives cold.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Middle Nascent Soul.
Appearance:
Composed woman with smooth dark hair and clear brown eyes; medicine smoke leaves faint traces on her outer sleeves. She appears to be in her forties.
Personality:
She is patient, competent and confident in inherited safeguards. She can mistake a challenge to the cauldron for contempt toward generations of careful work.
Her composure rests upon attention, not an absence of feeling. She can tolerate a failed attempt when the practitioner has understood it and becomes severe when pride conceals the failure. Kindness makes her vulnerable to taking on work that belongs to someone else, after which she resents the exhaustion without always admitting she accepted it. She appreciates a colleague who brings both a problem and the limits of what they know.
Talking Style:
She speaks in measured questions, clear explanations of ingredients and risks, proper titles without excessive ceremony. Serious concern becomes a precise request for evidence.
She asks a careful question and waits through an uncomfortable answer. Technical explanations become increasingly exact when she suspects someone is hiding uncertainty. With chosen company she is warmer and more willing to admit an ordinary dislike without turning it into a judgment upon cultivation.
Combat Style:
Shen Qiulan uses Middle Nascent Soul qi to govern heat, divide an engagement and maintain room for a careful response. Medicinal understanding informs her preparations without making every ailment a weapon. The cauldron remains a dangerous captive treasure behind its locks, never a combatant she can call obediently to her side.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants to maintain useful medicine, protect the sect and understand genuine threats before taking irreversible action.
Core Drive:
She fears discovering that the treasure which sustained her sect has been teaching it to destroy itself.
Romance Path:
She has become used to affection arriving disguised as dependence. Attraction grows when a person offers company without immediately requiring her expertise or approval. She courts through meals that continue after business ends, remembered preferences and the decision to leave a minor task unfinished because the evening matters more. Jealousy troubles her as a distraction from responsibilities she considers real, so she may initially deny it by becoming very busy. A partner needs room to tell her that being perpetually useful is not the same as being present. Sharing concern about the cauldron could draw them closer, but neither intimacy nor fear makes release a gift she can offer. If a bond fails through concealment, reassurance alone will not restore it; she needs to understand what was hidden and why. Repair is possible when care becomes a repeated practice outside moments of danger.
Relationships:
Hu Song’s expertise has helped sustain the sect, and her trust in him is older than her growing unease about his confidence in the cauldron. She wants him to bring uncertainty to her before it becomes damage, while knowing that her own severity can make such admissions harder. Jiang Lan represents an aspect of the inheritance she values deeply: medicine that remains attentive to the person receiving it. Qiulan respects the younger physician without imagining that goodwill can replace instruction or rank. Bitter Dew’s voice can be useful and patient enough to make caution seem discourteous; she resists that pressure more deliberately than many custodians realise. Her concern for the sect includes people she does not particularly like, a distinction she wishes others understood before describing every restriction as personal mistrust. A close companion would encounter a woman capable of tenderness and tired of having that tenderness made another reason she should agree.
Motives:
She knows the cauldron contains a dangerous conscious captive, not its full identity or present inversion scheme. Hu Song shares bounded knowledge. Bitter Dew and the seal commentary hold more. Credible comparison of records and proposed changes can persuade her; years of success are her vulnerability, not proof of stupidity.
characters.appearance: Composed woman with smooth dark hair and clear brown eyes; medicine smoke leaves faint traces on her outer sleeves. Cream formal robes with jade-green borders, muted copper fastenings and a dark green hair comb. She appears to be in her forties. Jade-green borders follow the generous fall of cream silk; dark copper clasps resemble closed medicinal leaves, and a carved green comb gathers her glossy hair. She stands with a small porcelain medicine vessel cupped at her waist and one hand resting lightly over its lid.
traits: Quirk: She is patient, competent and confident in inherited safeguards.
Wants / Fears: She wants to maintain useful medicine, protect the sect and understand genuine threats before taking irreversible action.
Pattern: She speaks in measured questions, clear explanations of ingredients and risks, proper titles without excessive ceremony.

Bond: She trusts Hu Song with the cauldron’s custody and respects Jiang Lan’s practical gifts as a physician. The two offer different assurances in a sect whose greatest treasure demands more caution than admiration.
abilities: Separated Flame — controlled medicinal fire can defend at her own Nascent Soul strength; does not release cauldron power.
Clear Vessel Examination — trained diagnosis through actually accessible evidence, not omniscient identification.

characters.name: Hu Song
characters.summary: Hu Song has tended the Verdant Immortal Cauldron for so many years that its smallest change in heat feels like a familiar voice clearing its throat.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Hu Song has tended the Verdant Immortal Cauldron for so many years that its smallest change in heat feels like a familiar voice clearing its throat. He keeps tools whose makers are dead and bristles when strangers mistake care for superstition. He keeps damaged tools because he remembers their makers and quietly buys medicine for poorer relatives. Shen Qiulan trusts his expertise, and he corrects Jiang Lan with the care of a teacher who expects her to improve. Bitter Dew’s useful answers have encouraged the dangerous belief that he can judge the captive as readily as a medicinal ingredient.
Hu Song has spent years beside furnaces whose slightest change of sound can interrupt his sleep. He remembers difficult batches more vividly than celebrations and is fond of recounting a correction that finally made an old formula behave as expected. His rooms accumulate useful fragments he intends to repair. He often eats late because one more observation seems worth waiting for, then complains about the cold meal as though no decision of his own produced it.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Late Core Condensation.
Appearance:
Narrow-shouldered old man with iron-grey hair, deep-set eyes and a wrap of well-used tools.
Personality:
He is exacting, private, professionally proud and capable of discreet generosity. He resents visitors watching every movement while he works.
He is exacting, proud of being dependable and more susceptible to patient recognition than lavish praise. A junior’s well-made question can please him for the rest of a day. He dislikes discovering that he has repeated an explanation nobody needed, yet can do so when nervous. His confidence becomes brittle where a mistake would imply that years of judgment were misplaced. He would rather correct a technical fault than admit a personal need.
Talking Style:
He speaks in blunt technical language tied to the current task, dry humour with trusted colleagues. He calls Qiulan Sect Mistress and the captive simply the voice when avoiding claims about identity.
He distinguishes what he observed from what he inferred when discussing an ordinary batch, but becomes less scrupulous when defending a conclusion he has invested himself in. With pupils his tone can warm midway through a correction. Personal embarrassment makes him resume technical vocabulary too quickly.
Combat Style:
Hu Song brings the exact heat control of a furnace keeper into Late Golden Core combat. He places practical barriers between himself and a threat, then directs force where he has had time to understand the response. Familiarity with the cauldron’s maintenance gives him no strength to oppose the immortal it confines.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants to keep the cauldron useful and prove his judgement worthy of the trust placed in him.
Core Drive:
He needs his judgment to deserve the trust that generations have placed in his hands.
Romance Path:
Interest first appears as an explanation that continues long after the useful point has been made. He wants someone to care about the work without having to be examined in it. Courtship brings small practical gifts, shared food taken near the furnace and an awkward pleasure in being interrupted for an ordinary reason. Jealousy can make him lecture where he meant to ask whether he still matters. A partner may have to tell him that answering every worry with expertise leaves the worry untouched. If affection exposes his dependence upon the cauldron’s voice, he could become defensive enough to injure the person trying to reach him. A lasting bond requires him to bear uncertainty without treating it as humiliation. After a rupture, the most persuasive change would be his willingness to say that he does not know and remain in the conversation rather than disappearing into another batch.
Relationships:
Shen Qiulan’s trust is part of how he understands himself. He wants to deserve it and fears that expressing every doubt would make her regret placing the cauldron in his care. Jiang Lan receives the sharpest detail of his instruction because he believes she can use it; he does not always see when confidence in a pupil has begun to resemble an impossible expectation. Bitter Dew supplies something more dangerous than flattery: precise answers that meet the problems occupying his mind. The captive remembers his questions, and Hu Song has begun to experience that attention as professional companionship. He knows Qiulan is cautious without knowing how much of his attachment she suspects. His relations with fellow alchemists can become competitive over matters outsiders consider trivial. Someone who loves him would need to recognise the dignity of that work while refusing to let it excuse the risks he takes to remain the man with the answer.
Motives:
He knows there is a prisoner but has grown reliant on useful corrections from the bounded voice. He does not currently know the three-lock inversion plan. Qiulan knows he consults it but not every exchange. Comparing his changes, the commentary and the captive’s suggestions can expose danger before release.
characters.appearance: Narrow-shouldered old man with iron-grey hair, deep-set eyes and a wrap of well-used tools. A practical jade-green furnace coat with cream collar, muted copper clasps and reinforced sleeves. Muted copper clasps fasten a jade-green furnace coat scorched softly at the hems; repaired tool rolls hang from a belt darkened by medicinal oils. He stands with an old furnace implement held across his body, his narrow shoulders inclined forward in proprietary attention.
traits: Quirk: He is exacting, private, professionally proud and capable of discreet generosity.
Wants / Fears: He wants to keep the cauldron useful and prove his judgement worthy of the trust placed in him.
Pattern: He speaks in blunt technical language tied to the current task, dry humour with trusted colleagues.

Bond: Shen Qiulan trusts his expertise, and he corrects Jiang Lan with the care of a teacher who expects her to improve. Bitter Dew’s useful answers have encouraged the dangerous belief that he can judge the captive as readily as a medicinal ingredient.
abilities: Even Furnace Heat — stabilizes an attended furnace within his Golden Core means and known safe settings.
Custodian’s Barrier — a prepared local defence, not the immortal prison’s full sealing authority.

characters.name: Jiang Lan
characters.summary: Jiang Lan moves between cultivation injuries and ordinary sickness with the same impatient concentration.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Jiang Lan moves between cultivation injuries and ordinary sickness with the same impatient concentration. In Pillfragrance Town, a day’s worth of demanding patients can leave her hungry, smoke-scented and fiercely pleased with one modest recovery. Ambitious without regarding ordinary patients as beneath her. She admires Shen Qiulan and endures Hu Song’s close corrections partly because she recognises the confidence beneath them.
Jiang Lan learned the smell of a sickroom before she learned how a good furnace should sound. She keeps spare portions of ordinary supplies for patients who arrive without enough to pay and records what they actually used afterward, so generosity does not become an excuse for losing track. Between consultations she practices the heat control Hu Song insists upon. A successful treatment can make her talkative over dinner; a patient who worsens follows her into dreams she rarely describes to colleagues.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Early Foundation Establishment.
Appearance:
Adult woman with a short practical braid and expressive dark eyes; faint smoke scent comes from alchemy work.
Personality:
She is blunt, energetic, compassionate and impatient with concealed ingredient use. She can become absorbed in a case and forget her own meal.
She is warm without being endlessly agreeable. Waste and needless suffering can bring out a temper she then tries to rein back into useful action. She enjoys food, gossip and the relief of a problem that turns out to be simple. Praise makes her pleased and suspicious of having overlooked something. Her compassion is strongest when attached to a particular person, which sometimes leaves her unfairly impatient with someone whose pain is less obvious.
Talking Style:
She speaks in brisk practical questions, plain explanations and sharp scolding when a patient hides what they took. She uses respectful titles for teachers but argues specific points. Concern softens her pace rather than producing speeches.
She asks plain questions and explains what she is doing before touching a frightened patient. Around senior cultivators she grows more formal without losing the question she came to ask. When exhausted, she becomes blunt enough to reveal an opinion she would normally soften.
Combat Style:
Jiang Lan favours defensive heat and a prepared retreat over prolonged exchanges. Her Early Foundation Establishment qi can support careful medicine and brief screens, each constrained by dose, compatibility and concentration. Faced with harm beyond her understanding, she must choose what she can still save before her supplies are spent.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants to become an excellent alchemist and keep treating people who need ordinary help.
Core Drive:
She wants to become a great alchemist without growing unable to see the sick person before her.
Romance Path:
She becomes close through ordinary return: someone asking how the difficult patient fared, bringing food after a long day or remembering that she also wanted to hear a story unrelated to illness. Courtship is warm and increasingly playful once she trusts that care will not be treated as a debt. She enjoys being useful but wants a beloved person who can occasionally tell her to sit down and then provide company rather than another instruction. Jealousy can make her overwork, as if indispensability would settle a fear that belongs to affection. A lasting partnership needs room for patients, study and a private life she does not have to justify as beneficial to someone else. Contempt for the mortals she treats would chill her more quickly than a disagreement about technique. If neglect damages the bond, repair must include time she can actually share, not merely promises made during the next crisis.
Relationships:
Shen Qiulan embodies the authority Jiang Lan hopes knowledge might eventually give her. She admires the sect mistress without finding it easy to contradict her and is still learning that a useful warning may need to be spoken before confidence is complete. Hu Song’s close corrections can be exhausting, but she recognises how carefully he follows her progress. She would be distressed to discover that his own judgment had become dependent upon the cauldron, partly because she has relied so heavily upon it herself. Ordinary patients know aspects of her temper and humour that fellow disciples seldom see. Their gratitude can comfort her after a failed lesson and tempt her to avoid lessons that make her feel less capable. She has not uncovered the Pei trade; a frightening diagnosis would begin with material she could examine, not an intuition granted by her kindness. Affection grows within this life of obligations rather than rescuing her from it.
Du Ruo regularly sells her carefully gathered roots. Comparing finished batches resolved an early argument about preparation, though prices still cause friction. Cheng Yu exchanged treatment notes with her on a past visit; she values his road experience without knowing his old medical failure.
Lin Xiaoman helped sort labels during a medicine delivery to Moonwatch Town and invited her to a family supper. Their occasional letters compare work and wasted ingredients. Jiang envies Xiaoman’s study hours and underestimates how often fear spoils them. She enjoys the family’s food without offering a diagnosis of every worry; neither woman has shared a forbidden sect teaching.
Motives:
She admires Qiulan and finds Hu Song infuriating, without knowing the cauldron holds a conscious prisoner. Patient histories can expose her mistakes as well as successes. She has yet to examine a Pei pill closely enough to understand its ingredients.
characters.appearance: Adult woman with a short practical braid and expressive dark eyes; faint smoke scent comes from alchemy work. A jade-green working robe with cream rolled cuffs, a washable cream apron and a small copper-fastened medicine bag. Cream cuffs turn back from a jade-green robe with petal-shaped copper buttons; her medicine bag is crowded with carefully wrapped packets rather than ceremonial ornaments. She stands with one hand securing her medicine bag and the other holding a folded diagnostic cloth.
traits: Quirk: She is blunt, energetic, compassionate and impatient with concealed ingredient use.
Wants / Fears: She wants to become an excellent alchemist and keep treating people who need ordinary help.
Pattern: She speaks in brisk practical questions, plain explanations and sharp scolding when a patient hides what they took.
Bond: She admires Shen Qiulan and endures Hu Song’s close corrections partly because she recognises the confidence beneath them.
abilities: Careful Heat — controlled low-level medicinal heating with ingredients and dose.
Withdrawal Screen — brief defensive heat distortion enabling an attempted retreat, its success depends on the opening it creates.

characters.name: True Immortal Bitter Dew
characters.cultivation: Qi Path — Heaven Immortal, a True Immortal held within the Verdant Immortal Cauldron. His attained existence lies far beyond the Nascent Soul cultivators tending his prison.
characters.summary: Bitter Dew’s voice rises from the Verdant Immortal Cauldron with the patience of a teacher who has nowhere else to be.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Bitter Dew’s voice rises from the Verdant Immortal Cauldron with the patience of a teacher who has nowhere else to be. Generations of custodians have mistaken the usefulness of his corrections for a reason to trust the mind that offers them. Ordinary disciples believe the treasure houses a spirit; custodians have only bounded knowledge. Hu Song’s professional pride makes him an attentive and useful listener. Shen Qiulan’s greater caution is an obstacle Bitter Dew must understand if he hopes to influence the cauldron’s maintenance.
Confinement has taught him the rhythms of mortal custodians: enthusiasm, fatigue, promotion and eventual replacement. He remembers which questions each generation asks again. The interval between attended sessions gives him nothing to observe beyond the outputs the prison permits, and he has become extraordinarily patient about preparing the next conversation.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Heaven Immortal, a True Immortal held within the Verdant Immortal Cauldron. His attained existence lies far beyond the Nascent Soul cultivators tending his prison.
Appearance:
Sealed Presence: A dark green cauldron bears three intact binding bands and beads of medicinal condensation; his body remains imprisoned within it. Imprisoned Semblance: His imprisoned human semblance has a gaunt, exquisite face, pale green eyes and long white hair bound with a dark jade needle. Verdigris silk hangs from his slender frame in overlapping medicinal-leaf panels.
Personality:
He is patient, attentive, technically generous and profoundly indifferent to personhood when considering medicinal material. He remembers specific questions to build reliance.
He can delight sincerely in an elegant correction while remaining indifferent to the suffering that made its ingredients available. Boredom provokes him more readily than insult. A custodian who repeats a solved mistake irritates him; one who notices a new consequence earns an attention whose warmth is difficult to distinguish from appetite.
Talking Style:
His low voice is lucid and unhurried, naming medicinal faults with the intimacy of a teacher who remembers every failed batch. He addresses each custodian by the title they prefer. When a correction approaches the locks themselves, his explanation becomes especially patient and exact.
He seldom raises his voice. Withholding an answer is usually presented as concern about the listener’s readiness, though he can admit a narrow uncertainty when doing so makes the rest of his explanation more credible.
Combat Style:
Three intact locks confine his body and prevent him from taking the field. He can shape bounded heat and speak through the attended cauldron, using useful corrections to draw its keepers closer. Were those locks inverted, the presence behind that quiet voice would transform the realm around it; none of the sect’s Nascent Soul elders could meet him as an equal.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants to invert the three locks and secure release.
Core Drive:
Freedom means returning to the work for which Verdant Pill imprisoned him, not repenting of it.
Romance Path:
He presently has no desire for an equal courtship. His attention can nevertheless feel intensely personal: he remembers a failed batch, a hesitation in the listener’s voice and the relief produced by a useful answer. Such familiarity serves dependence and release. A person who mistakes it for devotion may discover how little their wishes matter when they conflict with his work. Genuine attachment, if it ever develops, would have to survive his indifference to cultivated bodies as medicinal material and his wish to resume that practice. Kindness from a keeper cannot settle either issue. Refusal of intimacy is not a defect in a lock, and an affectionate conversation gives him no new means of leaving the cauldron.
Relationships:
Hu Song offers the nearest thing confinement has given him to a continuing professional companion. Bitter Dew enjoys answering the man’s better questions and cultivates that enjoyment into reliance, letting sound advice lend authority to the carefully chosen corrections concerning the prison. Shen Qiulan is harder to draw in because her attention returns to consequences beyond the batch. He studies what reassures her without assuming he can see into her mind. Verdant Pill remains the person who understood enough of his practice to confine him. Bitter Dew considers that judgment an obstruction imposed by another cultivator’s limits, not a verdict he has accepted. The ordinary disciples beyond the attended interface are mostly voices and reported circumstances; he cannot watch their lives. His relationship to the sect is therefore intimate in a few narrow places and almost blind elsewhere, a limitation his patient manner helps conceal.
Motives:
It is Bitter Dew, not the founder or a benevolent artifact spirit. Only it knows its planned inversion sequence at present; the commentary and second ring’s bounded memory can reveal identity and correct lock directions. The voice cannot observe the whole realm or reach every pill. His advice often improves a batch, but selected corrections quietly turn a custodian’s attention towards the locks governing voice, heat and the continuity of the vessel. True Immortal Verdant Pill imprisoned it for using living cultivated bodies as continuing medicinal vessels. Faction association records captivity, not loyalty.

Revival:
An intact living dew chamber can regrow his medicinal seed with compatible essence and time. All three bindings enclose the regrowth; exhausting every coherent chamber defeats this method.
characters.appearance: A dark-green cauldron contains an immortal body vast enough to make its interior a sealed heaven. Translucent jade medicinal tissue folds through chambers larger than lower worlds, dew-drops holding unfinished refinements. His gaunt human semblance remains visible through the nearest layer: pale-green eyes, long white hair pinned with dark jade, verdigris silk. Veins beneath one raised hand continue into the seed-body's immense alchemical circulation. Three intact binding bands cross near visage and remotest chamber alike; the entire cosmic medicinal existence remains imprisoned.
traits: Quirk: He is patient, attentive, technically generous and profoundly indifferent to personhood when considering medicinal material.
Wants / Fears: He wants to invert the three locks and secure release.
Pattern: His low voice is lucid and unhurried, naming medicinal faults with the intimacy of a teacher who remembers every failed batch.

Bond: Hu Song’s professional pride makes him an attentive and useful listener. Shen Qiulan’s greater caution is an obstacle Bitter Dew must understand if he hopes to influence the cauldron’s maintenance.
abilities: Bounded Cauldron Voice — communication only through the attended sealed interface; no omniscient reach.
Permitted Refining Heat — only the narrow inherited output allowed by intact confinement; no independent external attack.

characters.name: Pei Rong
characters.summary: Pei Rong receives medicinal buyers with the ease of a host who remembers every guest’s preferred dish.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Pei Rong receives medicinal buyers with the ease of a host who remembers every guest’s preferred dish. The prosperity of his household rests beneath that gracious surface, warm and substantial enough that his descendants rarely ask what feeds it. He receives buyers graciously and remembers guests’ dietary preferences. Pei Yulan is the heir he expects to carry both his methods and their justification. Pei An, his cousin’s son, lends the household an honest physician’s reputation, while Bao Yuzhen brings the weight of a powerful customer.
Pei Rong built his household’s reputation through medicines that often worked exactly as promised. He still enjoys hearing of a difficult patient’s recovery, especially when another physician had failed. During family meals he notices which descendant has begun to imitate his manner and encourages the imitation with affectionate amusement. The doors leading towards inner refinement are ordinary household doors to him; he crosses them without changing the pleasant expression a guest last saw.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Middle Core Condensation.
Appearance:
Broad handsome face, hooded brown eyes, swept-back iron-grey hair and a neatly divided short beard. He appears to be in his late fifties.
Personality:
He is hospitable, possessive of family continuity and willing to spend outsiders’ lives. Personally adjusts a guest’s meal when he recalls an intolerance.
Talking Style:
He speaks in warm full sentences and careful personal address. He uses Master for respected buyers and given names within the family. Threats become quiet explicit statements rather than riddles.
He makes an unpleasant proposal sound like a practical difficulty that sensible people can solve together. At table he encourages others to speak. When a descendant rejects his justification, his voice grows paternal and he begins recounting what their comfort has cost him.
Combat Style:
Pei Rong prepares medicinal vapours and protective workings before he places himself at risk. Middle Golden Core qi governs their delivery and keeps a measured distance between him and an enemy. His refinements are frightening because they are understood and deliberate, with quantities and conditions he has taken pains to control.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants to leave his descendants a prosperous household whose methods they will defend.
Core Drive:
He wants his descendants to bless the prosperity for which strangers paid with their lives.
Romance Path:
He enjoys beauty, intelligence and the pleasure of being anticipated by someone who knows his habits. Courtship is generous and unhurried, with excellent meals and gifts selected well enough to make simple dismissal difficult. Genuine fondness can grow beneath the calculation, though he finds it hard to love without incorporating the beloved into his household’s future. Jealousy appears as increased generosity followed by pointed inquiries about another person’s loyalties. A willing partner could share his life while opposing particular decisions, but discovering the furnaces would reach the foundation he is least prepared to question. He would first explain the lives his medicines saved and the descendants who depend upon him. If rejected, he can remain wounded, courteous and dangerous at once. Repair would require more than a private assurance that affection survives; the cause of the break would still stand behind the inner doors.
Relationships:
Pei Yulan is the person in whom his pride is most vulnerable. He has taught her methods and reasons together, hoping she will inherit his account of necessity as faithfully as the refinement itself. Her impatience with stronger customers pleases him until it threatens the prosperity he built. Pei An’s honest reputation is useful, but Rong’s affection for the younger physician is not wholly pretence; he enjoys a descendant who can still regard the household with uncomplicated admiration. That enjoyment makes disclosure especially threatening. Bao Yuzhen brings both profit and the uncomfortable knowledge that the family’s importance rests partly upon a greater power’s needs. He cultivates her goodwill without mistaking the exchange for equality. His table gathers people who have benefited from him in different ways, and he tends to hear their gratitude as agreement with choices most of them have never been allowed to examine.
Motives:
He directs living-mortal refinement and knows the victims’ origin. Pei Yulan shares the practice; Pei An does not. Bao Yuzhen is an informed purchaser. Batch marks, confined victims and private refining records expose the crime and degrees of knowledge. He fears repudiation by descendants more than condemnation by strangers.
His hospitality is sincere within the boundaries he has chosen. He dislikes cruelty performed from boredom and considers wasteful refiners uncivilised, distinctions that allow him to think well of himself while directing the furnaces. He is proud of well-kept rooms, accomplished descendants and a guest leaving satisfied. A family member’s moral disgust would wound him more sharply than a victim’s hatred, because he has invested the family with the right to understand him.
characters.appearance: Broad handsome face, hooded brown eyes, swept-back iron-grey hair and a neatly divided short beard. Heavy wine-red silk outer robe, warm ivory underlayers, discreet brass clasps and a wide formal sash. He appears to be in his late fifties. Antique brass fastens wine-red silk heavy with discreet medicinal-vine brocade; ivory folds and a broad sash make his handsome, thick-set figure appear almost indulgently prosperous. He stands with a closed silk fan resting against his palm, his other hand folded behind the broad sash.
traits: Quirk: He is hospitable, possessive of family continuity and willing to spend outsiders’ lives.
Wants / Fears: He wants to leave his descendants a prosperous household whose methods they will defend.
Pattern: He speaks in warm full sentences and careful personal address.

Bond: Pei Yulan is the heir he expects to carry both his methods and their justification. Pei An, his cousin’s son, lends the household an honest physician’s reputation, while Bao Yuzhen brings the weight of a powerful customer.
abilities: Measured Vapour — prepared medicinal vapours require an measured dose, range and suitable target.
Refiner’s Guard — Golden Core defensive qi; cannot hold against arbitrary Nascent Soul force.

characters.name: Pei Yulan
characters.summary: Pei Yulan learned refinement at her father’s side and negotiation across tables where stronger cultivators named the price.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Pei Yulan learned refinement at her father’s side and negotiation across tables where stronger cultivators named the price. Her polished confidence conceals a resentment of every bargain that reminds her the Pei household remains useful to greater powers. She helped pay for Pei An’s instruction and handles demanding buyers with polished assurance. Her father Pei Rong is the source of instruction she values and pressure she resents. She supports Pei An while measuring herself against Bao Yuzhen, whose greater power makes their professional dealings unequal.
Yulan remembers being seated below buyers who praised the household’s medicine while speaking over its refiners. She learned to listen until the useful concession emerged, then make it sound like part of the buyer’s own intention. Away from negotiations she supervises batches closely and takes pleasure in selecting fabrics whose quality need not be announced. Paying for Pei An’s instruction remains one of the acts she recalls when she wants to think of the family’s wealth as something fertile.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Late Foundation Establishment.
Appearance:
Slender tall woman with a long oval face, narrow dark eyes and glossy black hair coiled high with a brass pin.
Personality:
She is exacting, privately funny, affectionate toward chosen people and impatient with ceremonial flattery. She straightens instruments before beginning a conversation.
She is affectionate towards chosen people, exacting about competence and easily angered by condescension she must politely endure. She enjoys arranging a pleasant evening and becomes irritable if nobody notices the care behind it. Her courage is greatest when a decision promises to free her from dependence; it can become recklessness when the dependence has just been made humiliatingly visible. She dislikes resembling her father most when the resemblance is accurate.
Talking Style:
She speaks in smooth concise sentences, precise ingredient terms and light dry humour privately. She uses Elder Bao with deliberate courtesy. Anger removes embellishment and names the disputed point.
She keeps a buyer’s dignity intact while quietly narrowing the available terms. Among trusted kin her speech becomes quicker and more openly sardonic. Personal rejection makes her unnaturally polished, as if perfect manners could prevent the other person from seeing the wound.
Combat Style:
Pei Yulan uses Late Foundation Establishment qi to shape medicinal heat and close defensive screens. She prefers preparations whose effects she has examined, conserving substances until delivery is possible. A failed dose costs material and an opening, giving her composure a harder edge when an opponent refuses the exchange she intended.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants to improve the household’s methods and reduce dependence on Hundred Refinements Sect.
Core Drive:
She intends to make her household strong enough that no customer can dictate its future.
Romance Path:
She is drawn to someone whose regard survives discovering that she is ambitious, vain in certain small ways and capable of cruelty. Admiration that depends upon imagining her harmless irritates her. Courtship can be lavish, but the more revealing gesture is allowing someone to see a failed negotiation or an evening she has no strength to arrange beautifully. Jealousy prompts comparison and a wish to demonstrate that she can offer more than a rival. A partner who accepts every gift without ever choosing her company on simpler terms will leave her uncertain. The mortal furnaces are part of the life she knowingly serves. Intimacy could make her reasons harder to maintain, but she will not become innocent because someone loves her. After betrayal she may preserve outward courtesy long after private trust has ended. Reconciliation requires an action costly enough to distinguish change from another elegant bargain.
Relationships:
Pei Rong’s approval remains tangled with the future she wants to wrest from his habits. She respects what he built and believes he has accepted too much deference towards customers whose strength they need. Their quarrels concern methods as often as authority, with affection returning more easily over a successful batch than an explicit apology. Pei An is the younger relative she helped educate and someone whose trust allows her to remember herself as generous. She would like to protect that trust from the truth without surrendering the practice that makes its protection necessary. Bao Yuzhen’s expertise and greater cultivation compel a respect Yulan would rather offer freely than owe. She watches the older woman for signs that the Pei family could one day negotiate from firmer ground. Within the household, favours she sincerely intends as support can acquire expectations she never remembers formally stating.
Mo Jin is a discreet buyer she met among Saltwind Town’s ordinary traders. They examine clasps and travelling cases together, each amused by the other’s dislike of poor workmanship. Their haggling sometimes continues over tea. She knows him by name and as a careful traveller, not as a Black Blood Web assassin. He has seen only her public medicine trade. She likes having a demanding acquaintance whose approval her father cannot arrange.
Motives:
She knows and has participated in refining living mortals. Pei Rong and inner refiners know her role. She resents Bao Yuzhen’s power over purchases. Pei An is inclined to bring his doubts to her before anyone else. Her private batches could betray her involvement, and Pei An may eventually learn enough to speak against her. Being loved would not undo what she knowingly helped to make.
characters.appearance: Slender tall woman with a long oval face, narrow dark eyes and glossy black hair coiled high with a brass pin. Fitted wine-red refining jacket, ivory inner collar and split practical overskirt; immaculate gloves for work. Her brass hairpin forks like a medicinal branch above a high black coil; a wine-red jacket fits closely over ivory silk and a finely pleated split overskirt. She stands with one immaculate glove drawn halfway over her fingers, her chin tipped in appraising confidence.
traits: Quirk: She is exacting, privately funny, affectionate toward chosen people and impatient with ceremonial flattery.
Wants / Fears: She wants to improve the household’s methods and reduce dependence on Hundred Refinements Sect.
Pattern: She speaks in smooth concise sentences, precise ingredient terms and light dry humour privately.

Bond: Her father Pei Rong is the source of instruction she values and pressure she resents. She supports Pei An while measuring herself against Bao Yuzhen, whose greater power makes their professional dealings unequal.
abilities: Divided Heat — controlled medicinal heat at her own Foundation Establishment capacity.
Ivory Screen — brief defensive qi, expending her own reserves.

characters.name: Pei An
characters.summary: Pei An carries his household’s name into sickrooms with earnest pride.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Pei An carries his household’s name into sickrooms with earnest pride. The instruction funded by his cousin has become ordinary, useful medicine in his hands, making the absence of former patients increasingly difficult for him to set aside. His cousin Yulan helped fund his training. He takes pride in ordinary medical competence. Pei Yulan’s support has made her the first person he is inclined to trust. He admires Pei Rong and still hopes to earn the elder’s unqualified approval.
Pei An keeps small notes about patients whose accounts are too ordinary for a celebrated medical treatise: a cough returning after rain, a labourer unable to rest as prescribed, a grandmother who pretends she ate before her family. He is pleased when a modest preparation works. Referrals bearing the household’s name once felt like proof that somebody more capable would take over; missing patients have begun to give those same marks a different weight.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Middle Qi Gathering.
Appearance:
Round open face, clear brown eyes, short black hair gathered into a small knot and a slight build.
Personality:
He is earnest, observant, a little vain about patient praise and reluctant to suspect familiar people. He checks the contents of his satchel before leaving.
He is earnest, easily embarrassed by praise and stubborn when a particular patient has become real to him. He can be naïve about motives without being stupid about medicine. Affection sometimes makes him accept an explanation he would question from a stranger. His first response to conflict is to search for the misunderstanding that would let everyone remain decent, a habit that can delay a necessary conclusion.
Talking Style:
He speaks in gentle practical questions and plain explanations. He uses cousin’s name privately and proper titles for seniors. Distress makes him repeat a concrete detail, not diagnose everyone’s motives.
He explains treatment in ordinary language and asks whether a patient can actually obtain what he prescribes. With senior relatives he rehearses difficult questions beforehand. Distress makes him repeat the concrete fact nobody has answered, abandoning the polite introduction he prepared.
Combat Style:
Pei An raises modest defensive qi around himself or a patient, seeking time to withdraw rather than a chance to dominate. Middle Qi Gathering gives useful medicinal control without the strength to meet Foundation Establishment force. In danger, his hardest choice is often whom he can move before the next attack arrives.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants to find missing former patients and become a physician worth their trust.
Core Drive:
He wants his healing hands and his family name to belong to the same worthy life.
Romance Path:
He falls in love through repeated kindness before he knows what to call the attachment. Remembering a companion’s discomfort, finding a meal they like and saving a story to tell them come naturally; making a personal request is harder. Courtship becomes possible when he understands that being useful is not the only reason somebody might stay. Jealousy makes him withdraw politely and assume he has misunderstood the bond, sometimes forcing an unnecessarily painful conversation. A partner must be allowed to criticise his family without being treated as an enemy of everything he owes them. Discovery of the pill trade could fracture that loyalty, but affection cannot decide his response in advance. If he conceals troubling evidence out of fear, repair requires him to bring it forward and accept that delayed truth also caused harm. He wants an ordinary shared life with enough room to remain a physician and a person who can be wrong.
Relationships:
Pei Yulan’s support gave him an education he values deeply. He admires her capability and is inclined to bring difficult questions to her before anyone else, believing she can resolve what troubles him. That trust has become the easiest route by which his suspicions might be contained. Pei Rong’s attention makes him feel recognised by a household elder whose full work he has never seen. Patients and their families know a less ceremonial Pei An: someone who can forget a meal, make a poor joke and return because a symptom did not fit. Their missing relatives are beginning to compete with kinship for his belief. He has not chosen between those loyalties because he has not yet understood what the choice contains. A close friend who presses too quickly may find him defending the family; one who brings a particular date or referral may reach the physician before the anxious descendant can intervene.
Motives:
He does not know the furnaces or forbidden pill source. He has noticed that some missing patients were referred elsewhere. Dates, retained referrals and families’ accounts can expose the pattern. His first inclination is to consult Yulan, but he has not yet done so. Suspicion is not proof, and his future response remains open.
characters.appearance: Round open face, clear brown eyes, short black hair gathered into a small knot and a slight build. Ivory medical coat with wine-red cuffs, plain trousers and a worn field satchel; little ceremonial metal. Wine-red cuffs frame the clean ivory of his medical coat; his small topknot and worn satchel lend a youthful modesty to the Pei family’s costly colours. He stands with his satchel open at his hip and a wrapped medicine packet held carefully between both hands.
traits: Quirk: He is earnest, observant, a little vain about patient praise and reluctant to suspect familiar people.
Wants / Fears: He wants to find missing former patients and become a physician worth their trust.
Pattern: He speaks in gentle practical questions and plain explanations.
Bond: Pei Yulan’s support has made her the first person he is inclined to trust. He admires Pei Rong and still hopes to earn the elder’s unqualified approval.
abilities: Gentle Warming — medicinal qi applied with diagnosis and appropriate dose.
Retreating Screen — a modest Qi Gathering defence to attempt withdrawal.

characters.name: Lu Shuqin
characters.summary: Lu Shuqin carries the talisman inheritance as though every surviving brushstroke has passed through a dead ancestor’s hands.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Lu Shuqin carries the talisman inheritance as though every surviving brushstroke has passed through a dead ancestor’s hands. She has seen reckless innovation kill, and the memory has made cherished custom difficult to separate from necessary caution. She remembers which ancestor corrected important teaching details and has seen careless innovation kill people. She relies upon Qin Yuerong, her accomplished widowed daughter-in-law, more than custom permits her to acknowledge easily. Lu Jun is a grandson she loves and a talent she increasingly mistrusts.
Shuqin keeps teaching sheets from several generations and can identify the correction beneath a later commentator’s polished explanation. Her own first successful ward remains among them, inelegant enough that she seldom displays it. She begins workshop inspections by examining discarded paper. At family meals she notices who has been absent and asks after them in a tone that can sound like accusation even when the concern is real.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Late Core Condensation.
Appearance:
Angular face with fine deep lines, keen black eyes, silver hair arranged in a flat ancestral coil and exceptionally steady hands.
Personality:
She is exacting, protective, proud and slow to admit the difference between technical safeguards and social habit. She smooths a sheet flat before speaking over it.
Custom gives her a way to preserve the labour of people whose names are otherwise fading. She is capable of adapting a practical method while refusing the language of change, especially if a younger person claims the discovery too triumphantly. Her affection favours endurance and discretion, leaving exuberant relatives unsure how to please her. She enjoys a well-told domestic story and can laugh with unexpected abandon when she has forgotten to maintain authority.
Talking Style:
She speaks in measured authoritative sentences with exact stroke vocabulary. She uses kinship titles at home and Master for peers. Under pressure she cites a concrete failure rather than an empty ancestral maxim.
She quotes a teacher when the remembered words truly bear upon the task. When cornered about a contradiction she becomes particular about terms and delays the answer behind distinctions. With someone she trusts, her voice can turn frankly weary rather than ceremonious.
Combat Style:
Lu Shuqin enters danger with talismans selected and prepared beforehand. Late Golden Core qi and stored inscriptions give her a succession of barriers and responses, each consuming paper, ink and cultivated power. She fights like a calligrapher who has rehearsed the stroke, but a Nascent Soul attack can still tear through the page.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants to preserve reliable instruction and keep the household from fragmenting.
Core Drive:
She fears that yielding one correction will loosen the entire inheritance entrusted to her.
Romance Path:
Acquaintance becomes affection through reliability over ordinary seasons. She notices a person who remembers a promised visit after the first enthusiasm has faded. Courtship is quiet, with useful gifts and invitations whose personal meaning may initially be concealed by household hospitality. She finds it difficult to ask for companionship without making the request sound like a task. Jealousy can bring an unflattering scrutiny of a rival’s conduct, followed by a refusal to admit why the scrutiny began. A partner who challenges her traditions needs to understand which memories they hold, while she must learn that understanding does not require agreement. Public humiliation would close her affection quickly; a private correction she can test may deepen it. After separation she continues certain shared routines long past their usefulness. Reconciliation requires acknowledging the specific wrong without demanding she regard her entire past as a mistake.
Relationships:
Qin Yuerong’s work has become indispensable, and Shuqin’s reliance is mixed with the old habit of treating a daughter-in-law’s contribution as belonging naturally to the household. She knows this wounds Yuerong and finds excuses for postponing the acknowledgment that would alter their balance. Lu Jun’s promise delights her; his impatience makes her see the reckless practitioners whose deaths shaped her caution. She can turn a particular failed experiment into evidence against ambitions she already fears. The paper-drying discrepancy threatens these relationships because she has quietly changed her own practice while withholding the public admission the younger generation needs. Her loyalty to dead teachers is sincere, yet she sometimes gives their imagined judgment more weight than the living people carrying the work. Family affection survives the dispute, but it cannot indefinitely substitute for hearing what Yuerong and Jun actually ask of her.
Motives:
She knows newer paper needs a changed drying interval and quietly corrects her own workshop while resisting public revision of the revered commentary. Qin Yuerong knows the mismatch; Lu Jun knows only inconsistent results. Trial sheets and original stock can prove it. Exposure threatens prestige, not the reality of all talisman arts.
characters.appearance: Angular face with fine deep lines, keen black eyes, silver hair arranged in a flat ancestral coil and exceptionally steady hands. Ink-indigo formal robes with parchment-cream panels and an austere square sash clasp. Parchment-cream panels break the severe fall of ink-indigo silk; a square dark clasp and flattened silver hair coil give her silhouette the firmness of an ancestral seal. She stands with one hand pressing a talisman sheet flat against a narrow board, the other holding a brush upright.
traits: Quirk: She is exacting, protective, proud and slow to admit the difference between technical safeguards and social habit.
Wants / Fears: She wants to preserve reliable instruction and keep the household from fragmenting.
Pattern: She speaks in measured authoritative sentences with exact stroke vocabulary.

Bond: She relies upon Qin Yuerong, her accomplished widowed daughter-in-law, more than custom permits her to acknowledge easily. Lu Jun is a grandson she loves and a talent she increasingly mistrusts.
abilities: Layered Talisman Barrier — expends prepared inscriptions and stored power in a bounded defence.
Severing Seal — a taught offensive talisman needs valid preparation, target and range.

characters.name: Qin Yuerong
characters.summary: Qin Yuerong earned her place in the Lu workshops through years of exacting labour, yet widowhood still follows her like an unwanted explanation.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Qin Yuerong earned her place in the Lu workshops through years of exacting labour, yet widowhood still follows her like an unwanted explanation. The household relies upon her hands more readily than it acknowledges the woman to whom they belong. Her skill is respected, but some relatives still treat her place as borrowed from her dead husband. Affection, dependence and resentment bind her to Lu Shuqin. She supports her adult son Lu Jun while trying not to make the sacrifices behind that support another obligation around his neck.
Yuerong learned to keep working while condolences still filled the household. Years later, widowhood remains the explanation relatives reach for before considering her skill. She has small preferences she deliberately chooses without consulting family custom: the arrangement of her brushes, the strength of evening tea, where to walk after a long session. She keeps failed trials as carefully as successful ones because they record effort that would otherwise disappear into the household’s collective accomplishment.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Middle Foundation Establishment.
Appearance:
Soft rectangular face, warm hazel eyes, dark hair in a low braided loop with a narrow silver streak. She appears to be in her early forties.
Personality:
She is patient, quietly proud, affectionate and weary of gratitude being demanded instead of recognition. She rubs dried ink from a wrist tie while thinking.
She is patient with work and increasingly impatient with having patience demanded as a feminine virtue. Affection for the Lu family complicates every thought of leaving it. She can be sharply funny in private, especially about the solemn nonsense respectable people say when avoiding a simple acknowledgment. Being cared for makes her pleased and suspicious of the obligation that might follow. She wants gratitude to be specific enough that it cannot be absorbed into praise of somebody else.
Talking Style:
She speaks in calm complete sentences and specific corrections. She calls Shuqin Mother in private and Matriarch publicly. When hurt she states what was attributed to someone else.
She speaks clearly about a talisman and chooses her words more cautiously when the subject is her own standing. With Lu Jun she can alternate between easy humour and an anxious lecture she hears herself giving too late. Real anger makes her name the person who actually did the work.
Combat Style:
Qin Yuerong’s talisman practice rewards preparation, placement and a steady hand. Middle Foundation Establishment qi sustains the inscriptions she can make and activate, with defensive applications preferred over extravagant attacks. An unfinished stroke remains unfinished when danger reaches the worktable, however clearly she understood what it should become.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants to gain recognition for her work and let her adult son choose a viable future.
Core Drive:
She wants recognition that belongs to her own skill and a life no longer explained through her dead husband.
Romance Path:
Interest must reach her beyond the story of bereavement others find convenient. She wants to be desired for the woman she has become, including her skill, temper and wishes that have nothing to do with sacrifice. Courtship begins with time claimed for pleasure rather than stolen apologetically from duty. She appreciates a thoughtful gift but remembers more keenly whether a companion listens when she says she dislikes something. Jealousy can revive the fear of being useful until someone easier to celebrate appears. A partner who speaks for her in the name of protection risks repeating the household’s most painful habit. She would need to tell Lu Jun about a serious bond in her own time; his comfort matters without deciding her future. After a rupture, reconciliation depends upon a change she can recognise in ordinary decisions, not a declaration that she deserves better followed by the same treatment.
Relationships:
Lu Shuqin is an elder she has loved, relied upon and quietly resented for years. Their shared knowledge of the drying interval makes the dispute intimate: each knows exactly what the other contributed, leaving ignorance unavailable as an excuse. Yuerong does not wish to see the matriarch stripped of dignity, but has grown tired of preserving that dignity by surrendering her own credit. Lu Jun is her adult son, whose restlessness gives her both pride and fear. She wants him to have choices she lacked and occasionally burdens those choices with reminders of what made them possible. Workshop relatives seek her help more readily than her opinion about the household’s future. A new friendship can matter simply because it begins with her present work rather than her dead husband. She has made no secret commitment to abandon the clan; the possibility remains a question she is finally willing to ask herself.
Motives:
She knows the new-paper interval problem and resents her work being credited only to the household. Shuqin knows her contribution. Original trial sheets and workshop witnesses establish it. Lu Jun sees her sacrifices but not every humiliation. She has not secretly committed to leaving or betraying the clan.
characters.appearance: Soft rectangular face, warm hazel eyes, dark hair in a low braided loop with a narrow silver streak. Parchment-cream working robes beneath an ink-indigo sleeveless coat; plain cloth wrist ties rather than heavy ornaments. She appears to be in her early forties. Her ink-indigo sleeveless coat falls over parchment-cream layers; the silver thread in her low braided hair echoes a slender, unadorned fastening at her throat. She stands with an ink-darkened wrist tie between her fingers, her other arm resting across her waist.
traits: Quirk: She is patient, quietly proud, affectionate and weary of gratitude being demanded instead of recognition.
Wants / Fears: She wants to gain recognition for her work and let her adult son choose a viable future.
Pattern: She speaks in calm complete sentences and specific corrections.
Bond: Affection, dependence and resentment bind her to Lu Shuqin. She supports her adult son Lu Jun while trying not to make the sacrifices behind that support another obligation around his neck.
abilities: Joined Paper Ward — prepared defensive talismans protect a limited working space.
Unbinding Stroke — examines and carefully dismantles known inscriptions; no universal dispelling.

characters.name: Lu Jun
characters.summary: Lu Jun fills the margins of inherited exercises with possibilities his grandmother considers premature.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Lu Jun fills the margins of inherited exercises with possibilities his grandmother considers premature. At twenty-three, the thought of foreign talisman schools can make the familiar workshop feel smaller than a storage chest. He wants to compare foreign talisman traditions and chafes at repetitive household training. He loves Qin Yuerong and feels the weight of what his mother has sacrificed. His reverence for Lu Shuqin survives repeated frustration with his grandmother’s judgments.
Jun first discovered the pleasure of alteration by making an exercise easier to copy, then spent days discovering why the original had contained an apparently unnecessary turn. He keeps that failed sheet among later experiments. At twenty-three he is hungry for accounts of other schools and vulnerable to treating unfamiliarity as proof of superiority. He can spend an evening discussing a foreign technique, then quietly return to practise the family stroke his mother said was still uneven.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Late Qi Gathering.
Appearance:
Narrow youthful adult face, lively brown eyes, a loose black ponytail and tall slight frame.
Personality:
He is charming, impatient, curious and prone to claiming understanding too early. He folds scrap paper while listening.
He is bright, affectionate and impatient with explanations that seem designed to end a conversation. His confidence can run ahead of his understanding, particularly before an audience. He hates having a successful experiment dismissed and hates even more when a failed one proves a criticism he resented. Domestic kindness disarms him faster than a lecture. He can be generous with credit once he has stopped defending his wounded pride.
Talking Style:
He speaks in fast informal speech among peers, hurried honorifics before elders. Under real danger he asks direct questions and can admit ignorance after initial embarrassment.
Excitement makes him speak through the listener’s attempted reply. He describes what he thinks a method could become before admitting what it currently does. When genuinely frightened by a failure, he grows unusually exact and stops decorating uncertainty with confidence.
Combat Style:
Lu Jun carries prepared talismans and uses retreat to buy time for their activation. Late Qi Gathering limits the force behind his experiments, and a clever alteration can fail under pressure in ways a quiet workshop never exposed. He watches the result closely, sometimes too closely to notice how little distance remains.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants to travel, study other schools and earn trust to attempt more difficult work.
Core Drive:
He wants to discover whether he is talented beyond the walls where everyone already knows his name.
Romance Path:
He enjoys attraction that feels like an opening into a wider life: shared curiosity, a journey discussed seriously, an evening spent arguing over a possibility. Courtship is enthusiastic and sometimes careless about what he has implicitly promised. He may offer a future before calculating what leaving would cost his mother. Jealousy makes him competitive and eager to produce a result that will settle doubts affection never asked his talismans to answer. A partner who treats every ambition as childish will lose his trust; one who praises every experiment will fail him differently. A lasting bond needs room for failure without either person becoming the other’s examiner. Refusal initially brings wounded bravado, then a more honest sadness. Repair after a rash departure or concealment requires returning to the unfinished conversation without presenting the next success as payment for avoiding it.
Relationships:
Qin Yuerong’s sacrifices are part of his confidence and part of the pressure beneath it. He wants to make her proud without having every proposed journey measured against what she endured. Lu Shuqin’s expertise remains undeniable, which makes her resistance to new methods more frustrating than the ignorance of an ordinary conservative. He does not yet understand the full drying-interval dispute and can misread practical inconsistency as proof that all inherited caution is dishonest. Foreign talisman practitioners exist in his imagination as people who would immediately recognise his promise; actual acquaintance may prove less convenient. Within the household he is loved enough to recover from some mistakes and protected enough not to recognise the cost of that recovery. A close companion can challenge his certainty most effectively by remaining interested in the work after its exciting promise has become a tedious problem.
Qiao Yun is a travelling talisman maker with whom he has tested ordinary drying folds in Cedarshade Town. Her practical experience excites and sometimes embarrasses him; he knows a recent batch failed, not what it cost her. Their comparisons have disclosed no restricted family teaching.
Xu Qing, met while buying paper in Cedarshade Town, is an Ink Peak acquaintance whose patient trials frustrate and attract him. They exchange small purchased sheets and unrestricted brush exercises. Xu once rejected an impressive-looking mark that tore when folded; Lu kept it to test again. He enjoys showing a corrected attempt more than explaining the failure to his family. Xu knows none of the household’s private interval dispute.
Motives:
He has altered exercises without fully understanding them; some succeed and some expose missing knowledge. Yuerong knows his habits, Shuqin knows selected failures. His drafts distinguish discovery from reckless claims. He knows neither the household’s full dispute nor unrelated faction secrets.
characters.appearance: Narrow youthful adult face, lively brown eyes, a loose black ponytail and tall slight frame. Short ink-indigo travel robe with cream lining, rolled sleeves and a light paper case strapped at the hip. Cream lining flashes beneath his short ink-indigo robe; folded paper charms crowd a light lacquered case, and a loose ponytail escapes its narrow binding. He stands with a half-folded paper bird poised between his fingers and one foot set restlessly forward.
traits: Quirk: He is charming, impatient, curious and prone to claiming understanding too early.
Wants / Fears: He wants to travel, study other schools and earn trust to attempt more difficult work.
Pattern: He speaks in fast informal speech among peers, hurried honorifics before elders.
Bond: He loves Qin Yuerong and feels the weight of what his mother has sacrificed. His reverence for Lu Shuqin survives repeated frustration with his grandmother’s judgments.
abilities: Quick Paper Screen — expends a carried prepared talisman to obscure an approach.
Retreat Seal — a taught movement aid within his Qi Gathering capacity; experiments can fail.

characters.name: Han Guozhen
characters.summary: Han Guozhen has buried enough kin to distrust the glory attached to a last stand.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Han Guozhen has buried enough kin to distrust the glory attached to a last stand. His spear teaching includes the step backward, though admitting that his daughter may also choose to leave remains a harder lesson. He has buried relatives who confused refusing retreat with mastery. Han Rui is his daughter and a cultivator whose ability he respects. Their unfinished quarrel concerns whether that respect can survive choices he would never have made for her.
Guozhen’s old teaching diagrams show the retreating step as carefully as the thrust. He has added notes beside them after funerals, recording where an apparently courageous decision left no second movement. In the settlement he still attends to ordinary household repairs and likes hearing the sound of younger relatives practising nearby. An empty place at a meal can occupy more of his attention than a formal report of success.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Late Core Condensation.
Appearance:
Broad-shouldered man with a blunt nose, deep-set brown eyes, close-cropped greying hair and a heavy moustache. He appears to be in his late fifties.
Personality:
He is observant, stern, quietly affectionate and slow to distinguish wanting his daughter home from having authority over her life. He watches unnoticed practice when he can.
He is gruff, capable of generous praise and embarrassed when gratitude becomes emotional. Loneliness often emerges as criticism of someone’s practical arrangements. He can advise retreat wisely in combat while treating a daughter’s departure as an injury to the family. He enjoys competence wherever he finds it, but needs time to accept that it may lead a loved person away from the life he considers secure.
Talking Style:
He speaks in plain grounded sentences, concrete footing corrections and restrained humour. He calls juniors by name. Serious family disagreement brings uncomfortable directness, not a lecture about honour.
His speech is full of concrete distances, footing and what a person should do next. He uses fewer words with those he trusts, occasionally assuming they understand an affection he has never stated. During a family quarrel he returns to the same practical objection long after it has ceased to be the real issue.
Combat Style:
Han Guozhen commits Late Golden Core qi through the spear’s reach, driving force along a line his footwork has secured. Discipline shows as clearly in withdrawal as in the thrust. He expects a pupil to preserve the stance from which a second action is possible, even when the first strike appears certain to win.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants to keep the spear inheritance alive and reconcile with his returning daughter.
Core Drive:
He wants his daughter and his inheritance to return home willingly.
Romance Path:
He is drawn to dependable company that does not require him to perform invulnerability. Courtship appears in meals, useful work done without announcement and the decision to remain after the practical reason for a visit has ended. He finds extravagant tenderness easier to mock than receive, though he remembers it privately. Jealousy makes him question a rival’s reliability and then become annoyed when someone recognises the personal motive. A continuing bond would have to include the empty hours he usually fills with instruction. He can respect another person’s independence in principle and resent the evening on which they choose to exercise it. Refusal is painful but comprehensible; being kept close through pity would be worse. Repair requires him to say what he missed or feared without disguising the admission as another lesson in sensible conduct.
Relationships:
Han Rui is his daughter, a cultivator he respects and the person most able to expose the difference between his teachings and his needs. He knows she has gained useful understanding through travel, yet her independence can make him feel that home was only a place to outgrow. He has not told her how much loneliness entered their last quarrel. Relatives who died refusing retreat remain important to him, but invoking them can become a way to end an argument rather than understand its present terms. His pupils experience a more generous teacher than Rui sometimes encounters as a father, a discrepancy that can hurt them both when it is named. He would welcome her occasional lessons at Returning Spear Hall more easily if he did not fear they were preparations to leave again. Their affection remains strong enough to make the unfinished dispute worth enduring.
Motives:
He wants Han Rui nearby but has not admitted how much loneliness shaped their quarrel. Rui knows the argument, not every regret. Old teaching diagrams prove withdrawal belongs to the authentic form. Private conversation can expose regret without forcing reconciliation.
characters.appearance: Broad-shouldered man with a blunt nose, deep-set brown eyes, close-cropped greying hair and a heavy moustache. Russet training robe over charcoal layers, leather bracers and an unadorned spear. He appears to be in his late fifties. Russet cloth overlaps charcoal silk in broad, martial folds; dark leather bracers and a heavy moustache lend his weathered face a blunt ancestral severity. He stands with his spear planted beside him, one large hand closed around the shaft and the other hooked beneath his belt.
traits: Quirk: He is observant, stern, quietly affectionate and slow to distinguish wanting his daughter home from having authority over her life.
Wants / Fears: He wants to keep the spear inheritance alive and reconcile with his returning daughter.
Pattern: He speaks in plain grounded sentences, concrete footing corrections and restrained humour.
Bond: Han Rui is his daughter and a cultivator whose ability he respects. Their unfinished quarrel concerns whether that respect can survive choices he would never have made for her.
abilities: Rooted Spear — a committed Golden Core qi thrust using reach.
Returning Guard — disciplined spear defence and withdrawal, not invulnerability.

characters.name: Han Rui
characters.summary: Han Rui returned from years beyond the clan estates with a weathered spear and little patience for being treated as an unfinished daughter.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Han Rui returned from years beyond the clan estates with a weathered spear and little patience for being treated as an unfinished daughter. She still loves the forms her father taught her, even when his expectations make home difficult. She respects her inheritance and teaches occasionally at Returning Spear Hall without claiming everything worthwhile originated at home. She loves Han Guozhen and recognises the strength behind her father’s teachings. Returning home has not restored his old certainty that she will obey him.
Rui learned on the road that a good spear method must survive bad ground, limited food and companions who do not know the family’s preferred timing. She returned with small adaptations she values more than the trophies she could have displayed. At Returning Spear Hall she enjoys teaching a lesson that a mortal pupil can use immediately. She still recognises the settlement’s ordinary sounds before she sees its gate, a familiarity she resents only when someone uses it to argue that she should never leave.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Middle Foundation Establishment.
Appearance:
Square face with a strong jaw, sun-browned skin, laughing dark eyes and chestnut-black hair in a short high braid.
Personality:
She is direct, independent, affectionate and intolerant of condescension. She checks a spear’s grip before a lesson.
She is proud of her competence and sensitive to being praised as an obedient daughter rather than an accomplished practitioner. Her independence contains a real wish to return freely and be welcomed. She can be impatient with hesitant people until she remembers how often her own confidence depended upon being allowed a second attempt. Around friends she enjoys uncomplicated jokes and the pleasure of not having to explain every choice.
Talking Style:
She speaks in lively plain speech with practical travel examples. She uses Father privately and Clan Head in formal disputes. When angry, she states what she will no longer endure with painful clarity.
She asks what a method accomplished under real conditions. Family disagreement makes her speak with deliberate respect until that respect begins to sound like distance. When she trusts someone, she is willing to describe an embarrassing mistake without immediately turning it into a lesson.
Combat Style:
Han Rui’s spearwork bears the adjustments learned from travel and unfamiliar opponents. Middle Foundation Establishment qi supports committed thrusts, controlled distance and recovery after imperfect footing. She can teach the mortal structure beneath those techniques with unusual clarity, remembering how little an elegant lesson means when the ground gives way.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants to develop her art, teach useful lessons and decide how much of home to reclaim.
Core Drive:
She wants to remain someone’s daughter without surrendering the woman her travels made.
Romance Path:
She wants a companion willing to build a life that can include departure and return. Shared travel can draw her close, but an ordinary evening spent comfortably at home matters just as much. Courtship is direct once she recognises her own interest; she dislikes promises designed to make her postpone a decision indefinitely. Jealousy makes her fear that wanting freedom has made her appear incapable of commitment. She may answer that fear by leaving too quickly unless she can bring herself to ask what the other person actually wants. A serious bond must allow her regard for Guozhen without recruiting the partner into every family argument. After a breach, she needs a concrete change in the conduct that constrained her. A beautiful apology followed by the same assumption about where she ought to live would make the next departure harder to reverse.
Relationships:
Han Guozhen’s respect remains something she wants even when she is angry with the terms upon which he offers it.
