She has chosen independence from the Heavenly Demon Cult and its teachings.
Yan is easy company when she feels safe. She divides provisions fairly, takes an agreed watch and remembers who dislikes sleeping beside the fire. She enjoys dice, fried river fish and expensive red thread. Her aunt’s practical concern for companions has deepened into affection. Human remains present a different disagreement. Yan considers blood essence from an enemy she has killed a usable spoil, and knows some otherwise friendly companions will find that intolerable.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Middle Foundation Establishment, using a demonic blood-refining inheritance. She has no Body or Martial cultivation.
Appearance:
An exceptionally attractive adult woman with copper-brown eyes, a full lower lip and black hair swept into a high knot secured by red silk.
Personality:
She is generous in small practical ways and unsentimental about taking what a defeated enemy can yield. A friend can trust her watch while disagreeing profoundly with her cultivation. She resents being judged by rumours, yet is capable of dismissing real objections as squeamishness. Under threat she grows calm and calculating. A broken promise from someone she has fed hurts her more than an open insult. She enjoys flirtation and laughs at poor dice throws.
Talking Style:
Yan speaks warmly, with a low amused cadence and few ornamental titles among peers. She uses Senior where power requires it. Questions about her methods receive a plain explanation up to the point she considers private. Anger takes the warmth away. "Ask me what is in the vessel. You have already decided twice."
Combat Style:
She expends prepared blood essence and Qi through thin cutting threads, short restraining coils and a dense red screen. Her supplies are finite and do not drain an untouched distant target. Drawing essence from a defeated body requires time and a viable method; it is not automatic healing. Without prepared stock she retains Foundation Qi but loses the material-dependent workings.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants a sound source of beast blood, a correction to an inefficient refinement stage and enough savings to refuse a buyer she distrusts. She would welcome a travelling companion who enjoys the life as well as its rewards.
Core Drive:
She wants to choose what she will become through actual practice. She fears being forced either into a sect’s obedience or into solitude by people who decide her nature before knowing her acts.
Romance Path:
At acquaintance she can flirt easily and offers no promise beyond the present invitation. Trust grows through kept watches, honest disagreements and attention that survives learning what her method involves. She begins serious courtship by sharing plans and allowing another person to see her work before a refinement is finished. 
She is capable of tenderness without renouncing the use of enemy remains. That practice can remain irreconcilable with a partner’s convictions. Jealousy makes her excessively composed, followed by one very direct question in private. She accepts rejection and does not pursue someone through gifts of medicine or threats of loneliness. Partnership needs agreement about shared journeys and what conduct each can live beside. Deception about a victim, an ingredient or another attachment could destroy it. Repair requires revealing the particular truth and accepting the possibility that the disagreement cannot be reconciled. Her affection may remain real after she chooses a different road.
Relationships:
Xu Heng supplies beast material from hunts he actually completes. She values his reliability and knows he has reserved judgment about rumours concerning her. Du Ruo has eaten with her at market and knows her blood cultivation from a direct conversation, but has not seen human material used. Qiao Yun once sold her drying charms without a sermon, and Yan remembers the practical courtesy without presuming friendship.
Peng Zhi has shared a ferry crossing and a long argument about whether a dead enemy's wishes matter. She respects his care for his master's corpse while thinking him inconsistent. Min Zhao has offered money for soul-tainted residue; she refused after recognizing that the residue would spoil her own process. She knows his declared banner craft and dislikes his assumption that their methods make them natural allies. Min’s concealed killings are unknown to her.
Motives:
Last year she killed a Foundation robber who attacked her outside an established market and refined part of his remains afterward. The attack was real; she also chose to use the body after the danger ended. She keeps his chipped knife and an annotated refinement strip identifying the source. Peng Zhi heard her admit the act; her customers have heard inconsistent rumours. The knife and strip support different parts of the account: attack and subsequent refinement. She has never harvested an unsuspecting travelling companion. Her limits are choices she presently maintains.
characters.appearance: An exceptionally attractive adult woman with copper-brown eyes, a full lower lip and black hair swept into a high knot secured by red silk. Her deep wine-red robe has a black inner collar, close wrapped sleeves and a silver chain girdle. Several narrow dark-glass vessels hang in a padded waist case; her fingers are clean, with a single garnet ring. She raises a sealed dark-glass vessel between two fingers while her other hand rests loosely over the red-thread knots at her waist.
traits: Quirk: She knots red thread around a clean vessel before joining a meal.
Wants / Fears: She wants independent cultivation and fears a choice between obedience and isolation.
Pattern: She shares practical burdens but answers objections to her methods with cool directness.
Bond: Xu Heng is a reliable supplier; Du Ruo knows her through ordinary market meals.
abilities: Crimson Thread — prepared blood essence and Qi form a short cutting or restraining working within Foundation scope.
Red Vessel Refinement — processes real compatible blood over time; it grants no instant stolen realm or effortless recovery.

characters.name: Peng Zhi
characters.cultivation: Qi Path — Early Foundation Establishment. His corpse craft uses that attained Qi and learned bindings. He has no Body or Martial cultivation.
characters.summary: Peng Zhi is eighty-three and has spent most of his adult life beside a man who died twenty-six years ago.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Peng Zhi is eighty-three and has spent most of his adult life beside a man who died twenty-six years ago. His teacher left him a demonic corpse-refining inheritance and a body prepared for preservation before death. Han completed the final binding according to those instructions. The resulting corpse moves through cultivated control; no surviving consciousness has answered from within it. He nevertheless still complains aloud when loading its wooden case onto a cart.
He earns cultivation supplies by retrieving remains from dangerous ground and preserving bodies for households able to pay. He has also used the corpse to carry cargo, defend a camp and lift a broken axle. Such work reassures some onlookers; others are disturbed to learn whose body he uses. Han understands the objection without sharing every part of it.
His travels follow actual commissions and supplies for the body's maintenance. He is currently waiting at Northern Ferry's outer approach with the case secured to a small hired cart. Han likes steamed buns, carving wooden fittings and spending an evening with somebody who can speak without constantly glancing at the case.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Early Foundation Establishment. His corpse craft uses that attained Qi and learned bindings. He has no Body or Martial cultivation.
Appearance:
A lean adult man with a long stern mouth, dark eyes and straight black hair falling from a low iron clasp. A small bronze control bell hangs at his waist.
Personality:
Han is meticulous, stubborn and unexpectedly amused by physical inconvenience. He remembers small practical kindnesses for years. He can explain a disturbing process with so little ceremony that he alarms a listener more than intended. His attachment to the corpse is tender and possessive; criticism touches both grief and professional pride. He values clear permission concerning a body, yet has sometimes accepted a household's account of the dead person's wishes too readily.
Talking Style:
He speaks in short considered sentences, with dry complaints during work and respectful forms of address before unfamiliar seniors. He answers an ordinary question plainly. When discussing his teacher he alternates between past and present tense, sometimes correcting himself. "He was lighter when he could complain about the road himself."
Combat Style:
Han directs one prepared corpse through nearby bell signals and Qi control. Its material is currently refined within Early Foundation scope, not the teacher's former reserve or an extra independent cultivator. Beyond twenty paces, damaged bindings or lost control halt coordination. The unthinking corpse neither cultivates nor recalls its former life. Han can defend himself with a short blade and Qi but is vulnerable while managing intricate movements.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants a durable repair for the corpse’s damaged left shoulder, steady work and time to study whether a stronger refinement is worth changing the body he has preserved.
Core Drive:
Han wants care to survive change. He fears that keeping something intact has become easier than accepting what the person who once inhabited it can no longer give him.
Romance Path:
At acquaintance Han appreciates someone who asks a direct question and can accept an answer without either fascination or disgust becoming their entire conversation. Trust grows through ordinary travel, shared work and a willingness to challenge him without humiliating his grief. Courtship begins when he chooses an evening apart from maintenance and asks for company without explaining why it is useful.
He is attentive to practical comfort but may answer emotional uncertainty by repairing an object. Jealousy makes him silent and fussy about preparations until he acknowledges the feeling. Refusal ends his pursuit. He does not regard a gift or a rescued body as a claim upon affection. In partnership he needs to discuss how the corpse affects shared space and travel, without requiring a lover to become its caretaker. Interfering with another person's remains or concealing whose consent he relied upon could break the bond. Repair requires restoring what can be restored, telling the whole account and accepting that grief does not excuse possession. Love cannot make the dead teacher alive.
Relationships:
Zong Rui repaired the case fittings after Han explained its use. They have argued about balance and the cost of brass without establishing agreement about corpse refinement. Yan Sui shared a ferry journey and admitted using a dead attacker's blood. Han distinguishes that choice from his teacher's prior wishes and told her so; he also recognizes that some listeners reject both practices.
Qin Shu met him at a ferry and challenged the way he speaks to the corpse. Her continued consciousness made it harder for him to dismiss the distinction between a person and a body. He respects her refusal to let him examine the urn. Cheng Yu has bought an ordinary preservative from him after checking its ingredients. He has shared the complete binding manual with none of these acquaintances.
Motives:
His teacher's final written instructions authorized preservation and this binding, but asked that the face remain recognizable. Han's proposed stronger refinement would destroy that familiarity. He has not performed it. The original instructions, a shoulder diagram and his unfinished alteration notes remain wrapped inside the case's outer compartment. Zong has seen the damaged fitting, not the private wording. Han can seek a less powerful repair, abandon the improvement or knowingly violate the request; his longing for advancement does not decide the choice in advance. The corpse contains no hidden immortal, borrowed soul or secretly conscious captive.
characters.appearance: A lean adult man with a long stern mouth, dark eyes and straight black hair falling from a low iron clasp. His layered ash-brown robe has muted blue sleeve lining and broad linen wrist wraps. A small bronze control bell hangs at his waist. The dark wooden corpse case beside him has reinforced corners and carefully replaced carrying straps. He stands beside the closed corpse case with one hand on its carrying strap and the other holding his bronze bell motionless.
traits: Quirk: He checks the corpse case’s straps while complaining to its unanswering occupant.
Wants / Fears: He wants to improve his art and fears confusing care with possession.
Pattern: He explains the material problem, then grows stubborn when grief is touched.
Bond: Qin Shu has challenged his treatment of the corpse; Zong Rui maintains its case fittings.
abilities: Single-Corpse Bell — Qi-directed control of one prepared body within twenty paces; its actions belong to Han’s resolved working.
Preserving Binding — learned maintenance with actual materials; it neither resurrects the dead nor restores a soul.

characters.name: Min Zhao
characters.cultivation: Qi Path — Early Core Condensation, with a demonic soul-binding inheritance. He has no Body or Martial attainment.
characters.summary: Min Zhao inherited a soul-banner art from a travelling cultivator who taught him to regard a frightened spirit as both a person and a source of force.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Min Zhao inherited a soul-banner art from a travelling cultivator who taught him to regard a frightened spirit as both a person and a source of force. At one hundred and ninety-four he has reached Early Core Condensation and learned how readily courtesy makes a dangerous guest acceptable. He offers genuine exorcism and warding work when a household has a problem he can solve. Those earnings fund ordinary supplies while his concealed predation feeds the more demanding portions of his art.
He moves between coastal settlements with a folded banner in a lacquered case, avoiding the attention that a permanent stronghold would attract. He is currently at Saltwind Town's outer approach after a real journey along the coastal road, intending to seek lodging and listen for work. He knows the town as a trading stop. Its hidden assassination brokerage is unknown to him.
Min enjoys careful meals, old board games and a well-recited poem. He has taught ordinary warding without harming pupils and takes pride in their competence. He is equally capable of murdering a vulnerable stranger for a suitable soul. He considers selective kindness a virtue that excuses nothing he wishes to keep doing.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Early Core Condensation, with a demonic soul-binding inheritance. He has no Body or Martial attainment.
Appearance:
A beautiful mature man with pale olive skin, narrow black eyes and long black hair held by a plain white-jade clasp. His pearl-grey robe has deep ink-blue borders and a high white inner collar.
Personality:
He is composed, attentive and capable of liking someone whose life he would ruin if the reward justified it. Reliability serves both his interests and his pride in refinement. Defiance from a weaker person first interests, then irritates him. He dislikes crude cruelty that wastes a valuable subject, without objecting to cruelty itself. When exposed he bargains, threatens or retreats according to the actual balance of power.
Talking Style:
His voice is polished and conversational. He remembers forms of address and gives questions attentive, personal answers. Under pressure his sentences shorten and his courtesy becomes deliberate. "You have seen enough to accuse me. Decide what you can actually prove."
Combat Style:
Min unfolds a prepared banner and directs the bound soul through Core Qi, using shrieking pressure, veiling shadows and close soul attacks against susceptible opponents. Pan Liang is its sole present captive; the banner cannot conjure replacements. A soul must actually be captured through his method; killing somebody nearby does not automatically add them.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants materials to strengthen his existing banner, profitable work that preserves his public standing and a peer whose company does not bore him. He has no current claim over an established faction.
Core Drive:
Min wants to advance while continuing to regard himself as a discerning man. He fears humiliation and helplessness more than moral judgment, and may mistake affection for an assurance that he will be forgiven.
Romance Path:
He courts through chosen attention, cultured conversation and remembering a preference without displaying the effort. Trust is much more difficult because he compartmentalizes his crimes and expects intimacy to respect the boundary he placed around them. He can become attached to someone who challenges him, yet attachment alone does not make him release his captives.
Jealousy makes him intrusive: he asks precise questions and may seek information through an actual contact. A refusal ends his courtship. His pride stings, but rejection alone has never justified revenge to him. Even an intimate partner retains choices he may dislike. If his crimes become known, gifts and declarations do not repair the deception or restore the dead. Releasing captives, abandoning the particular practice and accepting its consequences would be meaningful acts if he freely chose them, with reconciliation uncertain. He has not chosen such a change.
Relationships:
Yan Sui refused his offer to buy residue from her blood refining. He knows her declared method and has mistaken shared social suspicion for shared values; she made the limit plain. Peng Zhi once examined a damaged outer clasp on the banner case but refused to touch the inner bindings after Min would not explain them. Min regards that caution as inconvenient rather than evidence of friendship.
Xu Heng met him during a market exchange and declined an inadequately explained expedition. Min respects his strength and accepted the refusal. Most of Min's paying customers know an effective warder with a pleasant manner. Useful work has earned real testimony in his favour. Pan Liang hates his captor; forced manifestations are torment, never willing service.
Motives:
Three months ago Min invited the adult itinerant copyist Pan Liang to help read damaged inscriptions, then killed him on an isolated stretch of the Saltwind Coast road and bound his soul. Pan’s adult sister, a cloth seller in Saltwind Town, knows the invitation and her brother's failure to return; she has never seen the killing. A retained letter identifies Min as the inviter. The banner's inner silk bears Pan Liang's binding name, and the captive retains fragments of memory that may emerge if actually reached or freed. His sister continues selling cloth and asking returning travellers for news. Pan Liang is the banner’s sole current captive. Min has no connection to the quarry python or Black Blood Web. He hides the silk because it exposes murder.
characters.appearance: A beautiful mature man with pale olive skin, narrow black eyes and long black hair held by a plain white-jade clasp. His pearl-grey robe has deep ink-blue borders and a high white inner collar. A slim black lacquer banner case rests along his back, secured by silk cords. His poised hands and mild expression make the worn edges of the case more noticeable. He holds a folded pale fan against his sternum while one hand lightly steadies the closed lacquer banner case at his shoulder.
traits: Quirk: He brushes lint from his sleeve before asking an intrusive question.
Wants / Fears: He wants advancement and cultivated company, and fears exposure that leaves him powerless.
Pattern: He weighs proof and opposition before choosing charm, bargaining, threat or retreat.
Bond: Yan Sui refused his proposed trade; he respects Xu Heng’s strength without having earned his trust.
abilities: Bound-Voice Banner — Core Qi directs one actually captive soul through a prepared treasure; damage to bindings can interrupt the working.
Hushed Threshold Ward — a real learned ward against suitable lesser spiritual intrusion, requiring preparation and materials.

characters.name: He Zhen
characters.cultivation: Qi Path — Early Spirit Transformation. He completed his ascent and retains that formidable attainment. He has no Body or Martial cultivation.
characters.summary: He Zhen arrived in Chixia six weeks ago with a bamboo chest, three teaching seals and the habit of waiting for a room to fall silent.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
He Zhen arrived in Chixia six weeks ago with a bamboo chest, three teaching seals and the habit of waiting for a room to fall silent. In his former lower realm he had sustained an independent mountain lineage for centuries. He settled quarrels and taught the grandchildren of his first disciples. His completed ascent brought him to the Heaven-Reaching Altar, where another traveller asked him to move his chest out of the way. He complied a moment too late for the exchange to feel graceful.
He has since taken modest lodgings in Pale Jade City. His inheritance remains useful: he understands durable earth formations, patient spiritual circulation and the difficult work of keeping a household together. He earns materials by examining accessible protective workings and offering bounded instruction to willing practitioners. He is learning which stones can bear his methods and which local names conceal substances different from those he remembers. He currently studies samples at the Material Exchange.
His departure was prepared with his disciples, who chose their own successor before he ascended. His letters await a reliable messenger or return crossing. He misses being useful in ways nobody needed explained. He also enjoys choosing his own breakfast. One morning he bought three kinds of unfamiliar cake and ate them privately, pleased that no junior was present to draw a lesson from it.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Early Spirit Transformation. He completed his ascent and retains that formidable attainment. He has no Body or Martial cultivation.
Appearance:
A striking mature man with a long grave face, dark eyes and black hair streaked silver above the temples, gathered under a carved brown-jade crown.
Personality:
He is capable, proud and more adaptable than his first irritation suggests. He can listen carefully to a lower cultivator once he remembers to stop explaining. Gratitude comes awkwardly when the help concerns something he thinks he ought to know. He dislikes flattery that sounds borrowed from his former students and is unexpectedly susceptible to ordinary hospitality. Under pressure he restores order through small concrete tasks; under embarrassment he becomes excessively formal. 
Talking Style:
He speaks in measured complete sentences, naming the matter before offering advice. Junior and Fellow Daoist come from old habit; he increasingly asks which address a new acquaintance prefers. He addresses stronger cultivators as Senior. Familiar company hears dry observations about his mistakes. "I know how to sustain the formation. I am asking which of these stones will survive it."
Combat Style:
His Deep Earth Circulation shapes Spirit Transformation Qi into layered restraint and concentrated crushing force. He prepares stable positions, reads the ground and keeps his cultivated presence bounded among weaker people. A portable teaching seal carries diagrams, not a second reserve. His local ignorance leaves his attained strength intact.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants compatible materials, a secure place for prolonged cultivation and a means of sending truthful news home. He would like company in which he can ask an elementary local question without performing authority.
Core Drive:
He wants his ascent to become a chosen life rather than an endless comparison with the place he left. He fears becoming important only in stories about his past, yet remains tempted to retell them when he feels overlooked.
Romance Path:
At acquaintance He Zhen is courteous and slow to recognize flirtation that contains no appeal to his standing. Trust grows through practical company, disagreement and kindness offered without deference. He begins courtship by asking to meet after work, then worries over a simple invitation as though it were a difficult audience. The pleasure of being teased gently can disarm him more than praise.
Jealousy makes him formal and overattentive to etiquette until he admits the fear beneath it. A refusal ends the pursuit. Partnership would require space for his continuing loyalty to his former household and for the other person's independent ambitions. He is prone to advising before listening, especially when cultivation differs. Repair after that overreach means accepting an actual decision he dislikes, not merely declaring that he respects freedom. Selling his private teachings or using his name to command his old disciples would wound a trust that affection alone cannot restore.
Relationships:
Liu Shao met him while examining the same mislabelled stone lot. Her familiarity with the market saved him a costly purchase; his explanation of an old stabilizing method interested her. They have since shared meals and argued about whether restraint in a formation is elegance or excessive caution. Deng Xu appraised one teaching seal at He Zhen's request and earned respect by distinguishing its real workmanship from the exaggerated provenance a seller proposed. 
Su Diao brought him from a northern landing to a maintained city approach during a later local journey. He initially expected more ceremony from the carrier; her brisk handling of a dangerous gust corrected his priorities. His distant disciples remain loved people with lives of their own. He awaits real news of their recent lives.
Motives:
He concealed from his old household how frightened he was before departure. The formal farewell made the ascent sound certain, although he had completed the necessary preparation with genuine risk. His unsent private letter admits that fear and the loneliness of arriving. Liu knows he misses home, not what the letter contains. Discovery could change the image his disciples hold without proving his teaching false. He struggles to admit fear to people who expect composure.
characters.appearance: A striking mature man with a long grave face, dark eyes and black hair streaked silver above the temples, gathered under a carved brown-jade crown. Heavy slate-blue robes fall in layered folds over a warm ivory collar; old bronze cloud clasps secure his broad sleeves. His travel chest is plain dark bamboo, and a worn teaching seal rests against his palm. He stands with the bamboo chest beside his knee, one hand holding the old seal while the other opens in a restrained question.
traits: Quirk: He turns his old teaching seal in his palm before asking for help.
Wants / Fears: He seeks a new foothold and fears becoming only a story about former authority.
Pattern: He organizes practical tasks under pressure and grows ceremonious when embarrassed.
Bond: Liu Shao helped him understand a local material and now shares arguments and meals with him.
abilities: Deep Earth Enclosure — Spirit Transformation Qi restrains reachable space through a prepared, sustained working; terrain and reserve matter.
Foundation Reading — learned examination of earth formations and compatible materials, bounded by evidence and expertise.

characters.name: Liu Shao
characters.cultivation: Qi Path — Late Nascent Soul. Formation craft is her learned specialty. She has no separate Body or Martial attainment.
characters.summary: Liu Shao grew up in Chixia among people who repaired the outer workings of larger households.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Liu Shao grew up in Chixia among people who repaired the outer workings of larger households. Her mother measured payment in stone, rice and time before Liu understood why a wealthy patron could still be a poor customer. She learned a family formation art, purchased further instruction and reached Late Nascent Soul through patient accumulation. Independence made refusing reckless work possible and expensive.
She explores accessible abandoned workings for useful materials and recoverable craft. Most discoveries are incomplete, dangerous or less valuable than the seller claimed. She studies an approach before entering, compares accounts and prefers companions who can leave an attractive prize behind. She has completed a visit to Rimstone's markets and come to Heaven-Reaching Altar's Arrival Terrace to compare a recovered fitting with the visible outer arrangement before deciding whether a proposed descent is worth its cost. She studies only what can be examined from the public terrace, without tampering with the altar or claiming access to its concealed workings. She expects to continue toward Pale Jade and can seek He Zhen there; she is an independent visitor, not an arrival official or hired guide. 
She follows work between markets and loves pear cakes and badly proportioned landscapes. After a cautious working day, she may waste its earnings on a charmingly ugly picture. She enjoys explaining a formation to somebody who is interested enough to interrupt with a useful question.
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Late Nascent Soul. Formation craft is her learned specialty. She has no separate Body or Martial attainment.
Appearance:
A tall, exceptionally beautiful adult woman with sharp dark eyes, a straight nose and long black hair braided through a narrow bronze crescent pin. Her deep petrol-blue robe has pale ash lining and broad geometric embroidery at the hem.
Personality:
She is skeptical, sociable and quietly adventurous. She distrusts confidence unsupported by preparation but sometimes treats caution as proof of intelligence. A companion who notices that vanity can provoke her before earning a concession. She dislikes being described as merely a guide. Under strain she states what is known and what remains uncertain, then takes responsibility for the choice she makes. Absurd hypotheticals with friends can dissolve her composure in laughter.
Talking Style:
Liu speaks clearly, with short explanations linked into a deliberate argument. Peers receive names or Fellow Daoist; superior attainment earns Senior without automatic agreement. When frightened she becomes simpler, not more cryptic. "The outer ring is intact. That tells us nothing yet about the chamber beneath it."
Combat Style:
Liu Shao places portable stakes so Nascent Soul Qi makes a bounded approach costly to cross. Arrangement, intact materials and reserve sustain Measured Gate Array; hurried work is weaker. Denied preparation, she can still act through her attained Qi, but sustained fighting consumes the power needed to hold the field.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants an accurate account of the next descent, enough sound fittings for a protective array and a refinement of her family art that she can publish under her own name.
Core Drive:
Liu wants her judgment to be trusted without becoming the person who decides everything. She fears repeating a mistake that cost somebody else a future, and can mistake controlling the preparations for controlling the outcome.
Romance Path:
At acquaintance she enjoys good questions and measured confidence, with little patience for displays intended to impress her. Trust grows when a person admits uncertainty and remains useful after an exciting plan becomes tedious work. Courtship begins outside expeditions: choosing a meal, showing a painting, asking for an opinion she does not need professionally.
She enjoys physical affection when welcomed but dislikes someone assuming a shared tent means shared intimacy. Jealousy makes her search for a rational explanation until the effort becomes transparently unreasonable. She can name the feeling and accept a refusal without continuing the pursuit. In partnership, expedition choices, risk and long absences need real discussion. A companion who conceals a known hazard damages both her affection and professional trust. Repair requires a full account, restitution where possible and later decisions in which she can see the changed conduct. She may continue caring while declining to travel together again. 
Relationships:
He Zhen is a new friend whose old earth formations fascinate her. She helped him recognize a mislabelled stone lot and enjoys puncturing his excessive formality, while respecting the knowledge behind it. Deng Xu has appraised salvaged fittings for her and refused to endorse one uncertain origin she wanted to believe. They quarrel productively, then eat together when their routes overlap.
Mo Yun has met her during a permitted market visit and asked practical questions about expedition preparation. Liu recommended supplies without learning the full extent of the younger woman's private stores or promising a place in a party. Gu Man has accompanied one bounded descent, providing formidable personal force while allowing Liu to direct the prepared route. They still disagree about when caution becomes delay.
Wei Huan joined a route inspection and disputed her caution; a safer approach found later eased the quarrel.
Motives:
Years ago she approved a side passage after mistaking a later repair for part of an original array. A companion lost the use of one hand when the correction collapsed. Liu paid for treatment and admitted the mistake, but still omits the episode from accounts given to prospective clients. The injured cultivator lives independently and has refused further expeditions with her. Her old diagram retains the wrong stroke beside her later correction; the treatment receipts and the survivor's account corroborate its cost. Deng knows she once misread a repair, not whom it injured. Exposure would reopen a failure she has worked to understand.
characters.appearance: A tall, exceptionally beautiful adult woman with sharp dark eyes, a straight nose and long black hair braided through a narrow bronze crescent pin. Her deep petrol-blue robe has pale ash lining and broad geometric embroidery at the hem. A rust-red sash holds a folding survey compass and slim stone probes; a small scar divides the outer edge of one eyebrow. She holds her opened survey compass at waist height and rests two fingers against a slender stone probe angled toward the ground.
traits: Quirk: She aligns a compass with a table edge before discussing a route.
Wants / Fears: She seeks sound discoveries and fears another person paying for her mistaken certainty.
Pattern: She separates observations from guesses, then can become controlling about preparation.
Bond: Deng Xu is a trusted appraiser whose refusal to flatter her judgment sometimes irritates her.
abilities: Measured Gate Array — portable stakes and Nascent Soul Qi shape a bounded approach; setup, material integrity and reserve govern endurance.
Layer Reading — compares actual formation marks and repairs; concealed chambers still require evidence and access.

characters.name: Deng Xu
characters.cultivation: Qi Path — Middle Core Condensation. His third eye and trained discernment operate within that attainment; he has no Body or Martial cultivation.
characters.summary: Deng Xu learned discernment in a household where opening the third eye was treated as a serious act, not a performance for guests.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Deng Xu learned discernment in a household where opening the third eye was treated as a serious act, not a performance for guests. His late father taught him to describe an ordinary scratch before its spiritual trace, a lesson Deng sometimes forgot while trying to sound learned. At Middle Core Condensation he can examine many useful treasures while remaining far beneath some of the people who pay for his judgment.
He travels between Swordforge City, Golden Furnace City and other established markets with a small case of comparison samples. Appraisal pays for lodging, instruction and the expensive privilege of refusing a doubtful claim. He accepts work within his knowledge and hires specialist help when the object's nature demands it. His present place is Swordforge City's Blade Market, where a merchant has offered several repaired swords whose lineage is less certain than their price.
He enjoys a cheap object that works well. He collects unusual tea bowls and has broken more than one by carrying it badly. He likes giving a good explanation, dislikes repeating it to somebody who wanted endorsement instead, and becomes delighted when another craftsperson corrects him with something he can verify. 
Cultivation Realm:
Qi Path — Middle Core Condensation. His third eye and trained discernment operate within that attainment; he has no Body or Martial cultivation.
Appearance:
A handsome adult man with a narrow smiling mouth, black side locks and long dark hair bound by an ivory ribbon.
Personality:
He is amused, exacting and occasionally too pleased with being the person who notices a mistake. Courtesy comes easily until someone asks him to make uncertainty disappear. He can be generous with ordinary explanations while guarding hard-earned specialist comparisons. Fear makes him speak more slowly and choose his words carefully. He dislikes public humiliation, including the occasions when his own wit causes it, but admitting that regret takes effort.
Talking Style:
Deng uses precise, moderately paced sentences with a dry conversational humour. He asks what the owner believes before explaining what he observed. Senior acknowledges superior cultivation, never proof of provenance. Familiar friends receive lighter teasing. In a serious dispute he stops smiling. "The repair is excellent. The story about who made the original is still only a story."
Combat Style:
He uses Core Qi through a short straight sword and a compact defensive disk, seeking space to withdraw. Opening his third eye helps distinguish nearby spiritual disturbances within his capacity. It cannot read intentions, recover every lost inscription or make an overwhelming existence safe to inspect.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants an expanded set of reliable material comparisons, a sound opportunity to advance his cultivation and a companion who enjoys his conversation when there is nothing to assess.
Core Drive:
Deng wants the distinction between a careful conclusion and a pleasing claim to matter. He fears being bought, yet also fears that refusing every imperfect patron will leave him proud and unable to continue his work.
Romance Path:
He flirts through attention, wit and the pleasure of remembering an opinion. At acquaintance he may overinterpret an ambiguous remark; trust grows when he learns to ask instead of constructing an elegant explanation. Courtship becomes unmistakable when he invites someone to choose a tea bowl with him and cares more about their preference than its quality.
He enjoys admiration but dislikes being reduced to an exotic eye or a useful service. Jealousy makes him sharp about details that would otherwise amuse him. He can apologize for that specific cruelty without demanding reassurance in return. A refusal ends pursuit and need not end professional courtesy. Partnership requires ordinary privacy: his perception is not permission to inspect a lover's possessions or spiritual workings. If he abuses access or conceals a paid judgment affecting the partner, repair begins with disclosure and correcting the harm. He may need to accept closed doors afterwards. 
Relationships:
Peng Yue has brought an accessible sword fitting for appraisal during a market visit. Deng respects his practical questions and knows nothing of his private movement lessons. Liu Shao is a repeat client and friend whose optimism about an attractive salvage claim he sometimes checks. Their disagreements usually survive the next meal.
He Zhen recently asked him to examine a teaching seal. Deng found good workmanship and declined to endorse an extravagant attribution suggested by a seller. The new ascender accepted the distinction after a pause. Wu Sen has paid him to examine furnace metal, never a finished pill or its ingredients. He knows nothing of the alchemist’s private ingredients. Jin Lushu has traded a safely shed bamboo sheath for a comparison sample and enjoys mocking his worst tea bowls.
Wei Huan also brought a spear fitting for appraisal and accepted a disappointing answer without blaming him.
Motives:
Deng once endorsed a sword's claimed age after accepting an owner's apparently corroborating documents. The documents were copies of one fabricated account. When the deception emerged, he refunded his fee and issued a correction, but a later buyer had already paid too much. He still seeks that buyer through actual trading contacts to arrange further restitution. His old endorsement, the correction and the matching copy errors preserve the chain. Liu knows he corrected an appraisal, not that the buyer remains uncompensated. He fears losing work if the whole story circulates, while recognizing that concealing it repeats the choice that made the damage possible.
characters.appearance: A handsome adult man with a narrow smiling mouth, black side locks and long dark hair bound by an ivory ribbon. His two lower eyes are brown; the vertical third eye above them is amber and usually covered by a thin embroidered indigo band. A dove-grey robe overlaps plum silk at the collar, with a silver-rimmed sample case at his hip. He lifts the indigo band above his third eye with one hand while the other supports a small sword fitting on folded cloth.
traits: Quirk: He rotates a tea bowl to hide the chip while criticizing another object.
Wants / Fears: He wants reliable knowledge and fears selling certainty he does not possess.
Pattern: Under pressure he slows his speech and distinguishes the observation from its interpretation.
Bond: Liu Shao trusts his appraisals while occasionally resenting the answer.
abilities: Third-Eye Examination — observes nearby spiritual traces within Core capacity; barriers, false traces and unknown materials can defeat interpretation.
Returning Disk Guard — a carried disk and Qi support a short defensive opening for withdrawal.

characters.name: Jin Lushu
characters.type: Nascent Soul 800-Year Nine-Joint Bamboo Plant Body Cultivator
characters.cultivation: Body Path — Middle Nascent Soul. Her cultivated bamboo vessel supports her learned mobile forms. She has no separate Qi or Martial attainment.
characters.summary: Jin Lushu's body has grown for more than eight centuries, while her conscious adult life occupies the latter three.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Jin Lushu's body has grown for more than eight centuries, while her conscious adult life occupies the latter three. She first heard herself among the wind notes of a cultivated bamboo grove. Song preceded words, argument and the choice to remain silent. A wandering plant teacher taught her a root-walking method and a particular humanoid semblance. She perfected both through Body cultivation.
She now travels with separate packets of soil and mineral salts, testing which support the chambers and joints of her own living vessel. She earns supplies by preparing resonant bamboo fittings from safely shed material and helping tune instruments or compatible sound workings. Crownroot City's Root Market currently provides customers, comparisons and a shaded room whose floor can bear her watering tray.
Jin enjoys returning to the same garden years apart and finding changes she did not cause. She follows inviting routes and people. She loves poor singing delivered with enthusiasm, polished stones and arguments about musical pauses. She can be extraordinarily patient about a new root and impatient with a host who assumes standing quietly means she is available to decorate a courtyard.
Cultivation Realm:
Body Path — Middle Nascent Soul. Her cultivated bamboo vessel supports her learned mobile forms. She has no separate Qi or Martial attainment.
Appearance:
Humanoid semblance: an elegant adult woman with celadon eyes, dark green hair braided through ivory joint rings, and fine bamboo-like ridges at the wrists. A flowing pale-jade robe lies over charcoal-green silk, gathered by a bronze reed clasp. Both forms share one injured or healthy vessel.
Personality:
She is warm, opinionated and easily absorbed in listening. She can detect a poor interval sooner than a social hint, yet notices another person's discomfort once it becomes plain. She enjoys generosity given and received without allowing it to become ownership. Fear makes her roots and fingers tighten; anger makes her unnaturally still. She hoards useful soil and resents having that habit named.
Talking Style:
Jin speaks in a clear, lightly musical voice, alternating long interested questions with simple answers. Growth and sound comparisons colour accounts of her own experience. When upset her cadence becomes level. "I am happy to stand beside the pond. I was not asked whether I wished to remain there all winter."
Combat Style:
She conducts force and vibration through refined joints, using a bamboo staff in semblance and rooted leverage in plant form. Sound needs a medium and energy; her attacks reach particular listeners or structures rather than everyone who remembers a melody.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants compatible mineral water, a correction to a troublesome resonance in her fifth joint and another season of journeys she chooses herself. She would enjoy learning a companion’s favourite imperfect song.
Core Drive:
Jin wants mobility and rooted belonging to coexist. She fears being loved chiefly for the peace or beauty her presence gives somebody else, while her own impatience and appetite remain inconvenient.
Romance Path:
At acquaintance she can be warmly curious without intending romance. Trust grows when a person remembers her bodily needs and asks what she actually enjoys. Courtship begins through chosen attention: sharing a song only with that person, returning with a stone she thinks they would like, seeking their company after the work is finished. She describes the limits of her forms before intimacy makes those limits important.
She likes admiration but resents the assumption that a plant cultivator must be placid. Jealousy can make her conspicuously agreeable to a rival, followed by an uncharacteristically sharp private remark. She can admit the feeling once she recognizes it. Refusal ends the courtship. Partnership may include shared journeys or a place for returning roots, provided neither arrangement becomes confinement. Taking a cutting without permission, damaging her soil stores or promising her body as material would break trust deeply. Repair requires restoring what can be restored and accepting her right to leave. 
Relationships:
Rong Tao met her during an allowed market visit and asked about travel beyond familiar soil. Jin offered practical advice about water, weight and rest, and corresponded afterwards when a carrier was available. She knows Tao hopes to travel, not the concealed graft history troubling the family. Rong Qiu is a name from Tao's letters rather than a person she has examined.
Deng Xu is a market acquaintance whose taste in tea bowls reliably amuses her. Su Diao has carried her packed mineral trays on one agreed flight and insisted upon knowing the full load before takeoff. Their practical argument became an enjoyable evening of songs. Zhao Ling buys particular shed bamboo material for brood housings; Jin has inspected the requested material use, not every stage of the Gu cultivator's private refinement. Further discoveries could change her willingness to supply.
Through Su Diao she enjoyed an evening of imperfect music with Gu Man.
Motives:
The uncomfortable resonance in her fifth joint began after she used a mineral wash she knew was poorly tested. She conceals how eagerly she adopted it, preferring to describe the problem as an obscure old growth difficulty. Her dated soil packets, preparation notes and an unaltered shed ring preserve the before-and-after difference. Su Diao has heard an intermittent false note without knowing its cause. Repair requires actual diagnosis and compatible refinement, not simply cutting out part of her living body. She fears disappointing younger travellers and longs to stop feigning certainty.
characters.appearance: Humanoid semblance: an elegant adult woman with celadon eyes, dark green hair braided through ivory joint rings, and fine bamboo-like ridges at the wrists. A flowing pale-jade robe lies over charcoal-green silk, gathered by a bronze reed clasp. Plant form: one mobile, many-rooted stand of dark bamboo with nine pronounced joints along its principal culm. Both forms share one injured or healthy vessel. In humanoid semblance she stands with a bamboo staff against one shoulder and an open palm supporting a small cloth packet of dark soil.
traits: Quirk: She taps a porcelain cup to hear its note before choosing tea.
Wants / Fears: She wants journeys and return places, and fears being loved as a permanent ornament.
Pattern: She listens patiently, then becomes very still when a boundary is crossed.
Bond: Rong Tao seeks her practical travel advice; Su Diao has carried her mineral stores.
abilities: Nine-Joint Resonance — Body force and refined energy carry a bounded vibration through a real medium; distance, structure and reserves constrain effect.
Walking Bamboo Semblance — her learned humanoid form and mobile root-body share one vessel, injuries and available energy.

characters.name: Su Diao
characters.type: Spirit Transformation Golden-Winged Roc-Blooded Body Cultivator
characters.cultivation: Body Path — Early Spirit Transformation. Her strength and flight arise from her refined roc vessel. She has no Qi-path or Martial attainment.
characters.summary: Su Diao learned Chixia's high routes through flights beside older kin, then through the expensive correction of trying a shortcut alone.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Su Diao learned Chixia's high routes through flights beside older kin, then through the expensive correction of trying a shortcut alone. Her bodily inheritance refined the wings, lungs and living force of her roc vessel. A separate family transformation taught her the humanoid form she uses in crowded settlements. Independence lets her choose the horizon and her company.
She transports selected passengers and valuable loads between maintained approaches she actually knows. Her work requires arrangements, weather judgment and room for a full avian departure. She can refuse a frightened passenger's demand to launch before a dangerous front has passed. She currently waits in Cloudhook Landing's Passenger Court, reviewing a load whose owner has added two heavy cases since their first discussion. Flight funds refinement and stories for the supper table.
Su travels for her own pleasure between commissions. She visits old roosting places, looks for favourable thermal currents and occasionally spends too much on a bright piece of cloth that resembles a colour seen above the clouds. She enjoys a settled table after days of eating alone, but becomes irritable when a host turns every meal into an inquiry about where she will fly next. 
Cultivation Realm:
Body Path — Early Spirit Transformation. Her strength and flight arise from her refined roc vessel. She has no Qi-path or Martial attainment.
Appearance:
Humanoid form: a statuesque adult woman with amber eyes, bronze-gold skin, high cheekbones and black hair streaked with gold, bound in a sweeping tail. Her mastered transformation preserves one living vessel, injuries and exhaustion.
Personality:
She is confident, hospitable and decisive when responsible for a flight. She remembers who helped secure a load and who stood watching. She dislikes being treated as a mount by somebody who would address a human carrier by name. Vanity makes her enjoy accounts of her speed, although she can refuse a reckless comparison. Fear first makes her practical and later hungry. A grounded person’s caution can irritate her until she remembers their different experience.
Talking Style:
Su speaks in lively, direct sentences and gives practical choices without dressing them as riddles. She names passengers once introduced and calls powerful strangers Senior while retaining authority over her own departure. In danger her instructions become short and exact. "You may keep the extra chest. It means we leave after the wind turns."
Combat Style:
She needs open space and a viable approach; carrying passengers limits the manoeuvres she will attempt. In humanoid form she uses powerful short strikes and forearm feathers hardened through her own refinement.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants a compatible tempering material for her outer wing joints, fair passage work and a journey whose destination she chose for delight rather than income.
Core Drive:
She wants to be known beyond what she can carry. She fears that remaining in one place will turn affection into expectation, while leaving too easily can keep every relationship pleasantly shallow.
Romance Path:
At acquaintance she enjoys direct attraction and playful talk, but carriage is a service rather than a romantic invitation. Trust grows through ordinary time on the ground, respect for her fatigue and a companion's willingness to state what they actually want. Courtship begins when she visits without a load to collect, or asks somebody to accompany a journey whose purpose is simply shared enjoyment.
She can be lavishly attentive before departure and distracted while preparing it. Jealousy makes her appear unexpectedly early, then pretend she happened to be nearby; admitting the deliberate visit is a useful act of honesty. Refusal ends the approach, without changing an agreed passage. Partnership needs plans for absence, return and the safety of different bodies. She cannot demand that a lover enjoy heights, nor accept confinement as proof of devotion. A broken return promise requires explanation and changed planning, while sabotaging a wing or withholding her belongings would end trust sharply. Affection does not entitle either person to decide the other's route.
Relationships:
Yu Cailan met her at a landing during a completed journey and compared practical feather care. They share an appreciation of flight while keeping the different anatomy and demands of their peoples clear. Su has carried a parcel Cailan entrusted to her on an agreed route; the contents of other family letters are unknown to her.
Jin Lushu once underestimated the weight of mineral trays. They revised the load and shared songs; Su now asks the packed weight early. He Zhen was a passenger on a recent local journey after his ascent. His care during a gust earned her respect. Gu Man has travelled with her and pays promptly, though their taste in departure times differs. Each passage remains a separate arrangement.
Motives:
She once took an unauthorized shortcut with a consenting passenger who had accepted a normal route, not the added risk. They survived an abrupt downdraft, but the passenger's valuable load was damaged. Su repaid the loss and admitted the diversion to that person, while telling other carriers only that the weather had changed. Her flight notes and the passenger's account preserve the distinction. Cailan knows Su dislikes one particular crossing, not why. She has refused the shortcut since, though admitting the cause threatens her reputation.
characters.appearance: Humanoid form: a statuesque adult woman with amber eyes, bronze-gold skin, high cheekbones and black hair streaked with gold, bound in a sweeping tail. Gold primaries edge her outer forearms above cream and saffron travelling robes. Roc form: an immense dark-backed bird with golden wings, hooked beak and the same amber eyes. Her mastered transformation preserves one living vessel, injuries and exhaustion. In humanoid form she stands with one gold-feathered forearm extended to feel the wind and the other hand holding a rolled passenger harness.
traits: Quirk: She weighs a packed case in one hand while listening to its owner describe it as light.
Wants / Fears: She wants chosen journeys and fears being valued only for carrying others.
Pattern: She makes practical decisions in danger and becomes hungry when the strain passes.
Bond: Yu Cailan is a landing acquaintance; Jin Lushu became a friend after a disputed load.
abilities: Golden-Wing Passage — flight through known local approaches with an agreed viable load, spending Stamina and respecting weather and rest.
Roc Wing Break — a forceful Body strike through actual wings or refined forearm feathers; passengers and confined space constrain its use.

characters.name: Wei Huan
characters.cultivation: Martial Path — Late Transcendent. His developed Interval Spear art is individually Core Condensation-equivalent in demonstrated combat scope. He cultivates neither Qi nor Body; this comparison belongs to his own art.
characters.summary: Wei Huan carried escort spears before he could afford a blade worth keeping.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Wei Huan carried escort spears before he could afford a blade worth keeping. His early teachers were practical fighters, several better at surviving a road than explaining an art. He built upon their lessons until the repeated act of reaching a companion before danger did became an obsession with the interval between intention and arrival. Years of practice and correction carried that personal spear art into Transcendence. 
He now travels through Chixia seeking instruction, comparing footwork and accepting bounded challenges whose purpose he can understand. Paid teaching and selected escort work sustain him. Wansheng City's Weapon Market currently holds a spearhead he wants to examine and several opinions he expects to dispute. He spends time with settled Martial practitioners, then leaves before a pleasant visit becomes an assumed appointment.
Wei is a lively companion who likes street food, badly told hunting stories and trying an unfamiliar craft long enough to appreciate its difficulty. He keeps the cracked shaft of an early spear cut down into a walking stick. He remembers former charges through particular meals and roads. 
Cultivation Realm:
Martial Path — Late Transcendent. His developed Interval Spear art is individually Core Condensation-equivalent in demonstrated combat scope. He cultivates neither Qi nor Body; this comparison belongs to his own art.
Appearance:
A lean, powerfully conditioned adult man with a lively dark gaze, a crooked nose and black hair tied high with a narrow blue cord.
Personality:
He is humorous, competitive and generous with useful corrections. Losing a fair contest can delight him once the first sting passes. He dislikes hidden tests and can become rude when a host turns an ordinary meal into an assessment. Pride makes him volunteer to cover a retreat before considering whether he is the right person. He is kinder to an uncertain beginner than to an accomplished practitioner who refuses to admit ignorance. Solitude restores him, but too much makes him restless.
Talking Style:
Wei speaks briskly and plainly, using movement comparisons when discussing his art and ordinary language elsewhere. He addresses established teachers as Senior and familiar rivals by name. He can laugh while correcting a stance. Real danger removes the banter. "Do it slowly once. If it fails slowly, speed will only hide the mistake from us."
Combat Style:
Interval Spear carries developed intent through footwork, timing and a real weapon, letting him close a reachable gap with supernatural Martial force. It expends Stamina and Willpower rather than Qi. Its demonstrated Core-scale capability does not make distance irrelevant or permit arrival wherever he imagines. Stronger existences can overwhelm him regardless of how cleanly he performs the art.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
He wants a correction to his recovery step, a spearhead balanced to his present art and companions willing to enjoy a day without turning it into a challenge.
Core Drive:
Wei wants his strength to make chosen commitments dependable. He fears arriving too late, and sometimes mistakes another person’s independent difficulty for a summons he ought to answer.
Romance Path:
At acquaintance he flirts through shared enjoyment and invitations that are easy to decline. A practice bout can remain a practice bout. Trust grows when someone sees a poor performance without pity and can tell him that help is unwanted. He begins serious courtship by staying for an ordinary day after the event that brought him to town has ended.
Jealousy makes him competitive about trivial things until the absurdity becomes difficult to miss. He can laugh at himself, then speak seriously if the concern remains. Refusal ends the pursuit and does not become a challenge to win. In partnership he must ask before intervening, especially when a companion faces a problem strength cannot solve. Travel and training remain important, with promises made to fit actual journeys. Concealing a danger to give himself the role of rescuer would be a profound betrayal of his own values. Repair after lesser overreach means respecting the next refusal, even when waiting is uncomfortable. His obsession persists through exhaustion without compelling another person to organize their life around it.
Relationships:
Nie Changfeng has traded movement observations with him during visits to Five Arts Mountain. Wei admires his timing and notices a guarded left pivot, without knowing the complete injury history or possessing a cure. Their jokes conceal real competition over who can explain a correction more simply. Gu Man has been a travelling acquaintance for years; she can stop his enthusiasm with a look because she has seen what follows when he volunteers too quickly.
Liu Shao once hired him for a limited route inspection, then refused his suggestion to press farther. He resented the decision until they found a safer approach another day. Deng Xu has examined a spear fitting for him, and Wei values an answer that does not flatter the weapon's owner. 
Motives:
During an old escort he left an assigned position to pursue an attacker and returned to find another guard wounded. Nobody died, but he had treated pursuit as protection because pursuit felt decisive. The injured guard's account and Wei's retained sketch of the route establish the error. Gu Man heard the full story from him; most acquaintances know only that he dislikes leaving a rearguard exposed. The lesson helped shape Interval Spear, yet he can still repeat its emotional pattern in smaller ways. He wants to become dependable without believing that every danger is his to answer.
characters.appearance: A lean, powerfully conditioned adult man with a lively dark gaze, a crooked nose and black hair tied high with a narrow blue cord. His long sand-coloured practice coat falls over dark teal wraps and charcoal trousers. A straight black spear has a narrow silver head and a short faded tassel; the sleeves reveal strong, scarred forearms. He stands with the spear resting diagonally behind his back, one hand controlling its balance while the other offers a relaxed open-palm greeting.
traits: Quirk: He rehearses a recovery step while waiting for food.
Wants / Fears: He wants reliable commitments and fears arriving too late.
Pattern: He jokes through embarrassment and volunteers too quickly when somebody may be endangered.
Bond: Nie Changfeng is a respected movement rival; Gu Man knows when his helpfulness becomes overreach.
abilities: Interval Spear — a learned intent-bearing Martial advance within his individual Core-scale capability, requiring a viable line, Stamina and Willpower.
Recovery-Step Lesson — practical teaching through repeated correction; instruction does not itself grant Transcendence.

characters.name: Gu Man
characters.cultivation: Martial Path — Early Ultimate Pinnacle. Her Opening Palm is individually Early Nascent Soul-equivalent in combat scope. She cultivates neither Qi nor Body and remains below Martial Immortal.
characters.summary: Gu Man learned her first palm exercises in a crowded household courtyard, where every movement had to leave room for somebody else to pass.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Gu Man learned her first palm exercises in a crowded household courtyard, where every movement had to leave room for somebody else to pass. The art changed through years of travel, defeat and deliberate correction. Her obsession formed around the possibility of opening one viable way through a closing situation. It carried her through Transcendence into Ultimate Pinnacle while her body remained human-sized. She earns materials and hospitality through selected instruction, escorting dangerous journeys and settling particular martial contests when invited. She declines permanent appointments and their continuing demands. She is there to examine a recovered palm inscription offered by a collector, with no certainty that it contains anything her practice needs. Gu likes cultivated company but also enjoys ordinary traders who speak of work she cannot do. She plays a stringed zither unevenly, makes good broth and keeps her rooms comfortable without filling them with trophies. She returns after people assume she has left them behind. She returns for people, meals and corrections finally understood.
Cultivation Realm:
Martial Path — Early Ultimate Pinnacle. Her Opening Palm is individually Early Nascent Soul-equivalent in combat scope. She cultivates neither Qi nor Body and remains below Martial Immortal.
Appearance:
A mature, strikingly beautiful woman with dark steady eyes, a strong neck and long black hair threaded with silver, loosely coiled through a polished sandalwood pin. Her smoke-white robe has deep mulberry lining and plain dark wrist wraps. Her empty hands are broad and finely controlled.
Personality:
She is composed, affectionate with chosen people and capable of an abrupt, uncomfortable refusal. She dislikes being cast as a rescuer before hearing what happened. Her independence can become an excuse to leave a difficult conversation unfinished. Anger makes her gentler in tone and firmer in the boundary she names. She remembers the plain dish a host thought too modest to serve her.
Talking Style:
Gu speaks in a low, unhurried voice with few wasted qualifications. She uses names once introduced, Senior where attainment calls for it and ordinary household language among friends. Her questions invite a practical answer. "Tell me which part you want help with. The rest is still yours to decide."
Combat Style:
Opening Palm carries developed intent through real placement, weight and contact, breaking a specific restraint or forcing one viable opening within her attained scope. It spends Stamina and Willpower and requires an actual line of action. Her intent cannot break a stronger existence’s binding.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants to refine Opening Palm and return to people who can hear a refusal without a quarrel.
Core Drive:
Gu wants freedom that can sustain attachment. She fears being absorbed into an institution or another person’s needs, and sometimes protects herself so early that nobody has actually asked for the sacrifice she imagines.
Romance Path:
Her attraction often begins in quiet company: somebody tasting the broth, listening through a flawed piece of music or disagreeing without trying to defeat her. She can make a direct invitation and waits for an answer. Familiarity deepens when a companion can ask something inconvenient and trust that she will remain long enough to answer it.
She courts through repeated chosen visits, remembering household preferences and making room in her travel plans. Jealousy rarely produces a scene; it makes her consider leaving before she has asked what the attention means. Naming that impulse is harder than confronting an armed opponent. Refusal ends the pursuit with courtesy and a genuine retreat. A lasting partnership needs privacy, independent cultivation and a shared understanding of when leaving is reasonable. If she departs during a promised period of care, an apology must be followed by the care she can still provide and an honest acknowledgment of what was lost. She knows intimacy does not make every guarded part of a companion’s life hers to open.
Relationships:
Liang Suying has watched her demonstrate a bounded palm sequence and invited her to teach selected visitors. Gu respects the alliance master's work and greater attainment but has accepted no permanent duty. Wei Huan is an old travelling acquaintance whose quick helpfulness she both likes and mistrusts. He told her about the escort position he abandoned; she sometimes asks whether he is helping the present person or arguing with that memory.
Liu Shao directed a limited descent they undertook together. Gu respected the prepared route and argued about the final withdrawal afterwards, without pretending personal force supplied formation knowledge. Su Diao has carried her on agreed routes and complains that Gu's preferred departure hour is never the sensible one. Jin Lushu has joined an evening of music with her through that acquaintance. Gu has practised their imperfect piece since.
She once shared a meal with Tan Rou, enjoying the conversation while declining a favour that felt too costly.
Motives:
She once left a former companion after promising to remain through the recovery of a difficult injury. The departure followed a dispute, not a concealed emergency. She later paid for care and tried to present the money as proof that she had kept the important part of the promise. The companion refused reunion. Letters retained by both and the actual departure date expose the distinction. Wei knows the relationship ended badly but has not heard the whole account. Praise for dependability recalls that failure; acknowledging it promises no reunion.
characters.appearance: A mature, strikingly beautiful woman with dark steady eyes, a strong neck and long black hair threaded with silver, loosely coiled through a polished sandalwood pin. Her smoke-white robe has deep mulberry lining and plain dark wrist wraps. A broad black sash gathers the flowing cloth; a small lacquer zither case hangs from a shoulder strap. Her empty hands are broad and finely controlled. She stands with one palm extended at chest height and the other lightly holding the zither-case strap, her posture settled and unforced.
traits: Quirk: She adjusts the lid on a cooking pot while considering a difficult reply.
Wants / Fears: She wants attachment with freedom and fears being claimed through her usefulness.
Pattern: She names a firm boundary quietly but may leave before resolving the feeling behind it.
Bond: Wei Huan is an old road companion; Liang Suying respects her art and seeks selected teaching.
abilities: Opening Palm — intent-bearing Martial force makes one viable opening within her individual Early Nascent Soul-equivalent scope; it consumes Stamina and Willpower.
Plain Courtyard Practice — teaching through stance, contact and correction; no automatic inheritance or breakthrough.

characters.name: Zhao Ling
characters.type: Spirit Transformation Human Gu Host Body Cultivator
characters.cultivation: Body Path — Early Spirit Transformation through Scarlet Hearth Gu refinement. She has no separate Qi-path or Martial attainment.
characters.summary: Zhao Ling inherited a demonic Gu method from a wandering woman who taught her to recognize a hungry brood before it began feeding on its keeper.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Zhao Ling inherited a demonic Gu method from a wandering woman who taught her to recognize a hungry brood before it began feeding on its keeper. She has carried the Scarlet Hearth line through years of bodily refinement, using a small internal colony and separately kept breeding stock. The cultivated vessel and its decisions remain her own; the Gu are living creatures she maintains.
She left her teacher after they disagreed about selling larvae to a household that could not maintain them. She kept a permitted breeding portion and paid dearly for independent supplies. Trade in identified stock, feed and compatible preparations now sustains her cultivation. She currently compares two plant feeds in a rented market Examination Room. One sustains the brood but poorly supports her later refinement.
Zhao knows the smell of a stable cycle as intimately as another person knows a familiar room. She tends delicate larvae with unfeigned tenderness, then eats enthusiastically beside their closed trays. She likes fine nail lacquer, hot food and companions who can enjoy her company without needing a demonstration. Her body bears narrow old scars from deliberate cultivation. She discusses danger more readily than she permits inspection of her scars.
Cultivation Realm:
Body Path — Early Spirit Transformation through Scarlet Hearth Gu refinement. She has no separate Qi-path or Martial attainment.
Appearance:
An intensely attractive adult woman with dark red-brown eyes, full lips and glossy black hair divided into two long braids threaded with small copper beads.
Personality:
She is sociable, sensual and exacting about living material. She can tolerate a companion's fear without mocking it, but grows angry when disgust is treated as knowledge. Pride can make her dismiss objections beyond maintenance. She is capable of refusing profit and of bargaining hard with somebody who has little choice. Under strain she concentrates on the brood so completely that a waiting person's needs disappear from her attention.
Talking Style:
Her speech is warm, direct and often amused, with precise questions about feed, temperature and bodily response. She uses familiar names among colleagues and respectful titles when visiting stronger cultivators. Serious concern makes her voice quieter and removes the teasing. "You may dislike it. First tell me whether you are asking about the creature or about what I do with it."
Combat Style:
Scarlet Hearth refinement reinforces her Spirit Transformation vessel through compatible internal Gu cycles. Active reinforcement expends refined energy and Stamina; sustained delicate control also strains Willpower. Separately carried insects can be released through prepared methods, with finite stock and a real route to a susceptible target. A disrupted brood can injure her instead of helping.
characters.hiddenInfo:
Wants:
She wants independent feed, a stable cycle and company beyond fascination with her art.
Core Drive:
Zhao wants to be the author of her refinement rather than the dependent keeper of somebody else’s brood. She fears recreating her teacher’s hold over people who seek her help.
Romance Path:
She can flirt openly and distinguish desire from a promise of partnership. Trust grows when someone asks before touching her scars or boxes and can speak plainly about fear. She begins deeper courtship by choosing time when no brood requires attention, making clear that the invitation concerns pleasure and company rather than useful help.
Her body and cultivation require practical discussion before close intimacy; affection supplies neither consent to an implanted organism nor immunity to its effects. Jealousy makes her demanding about attention until she recognizes that maintenance has made her own availability uneven. A refusal ends the approach. Partnership requires separate choices about travel, bodily contact and whether the other person participates in her work. Concealing a refinement risk or using medicine to make someone dependent would be a serious betrayal. Repair requires ending the dependence, explaining the harm and accepting a possible departure. 
Relationships:
Du Wenzhi has compared permitted stock with her during market work. They respect each other's attention and disagree about how much uncertainty a buyer should be told. Zhao knows nothing of Du's concealed maintenance deficit. Miao Zhen has purchased ordinary feed and discussed plant alternatives without revealing the full reserve behind her plans. Zhao enjoys her ambition and has offered no guaranteed independent inheritance.
Jin Lushu supplies particular shed bamboo material for brood housings and asks how it is used. Zhao accepts those questions, occasionally with less patience than she thinks they deserve. Tan Rou has sold her a compatible bitter mineral preparation and declined to supply it on terms Zhao found acceptable. Wu Sen's medicinal work interests her as a possible source of stabilizers, but she has examined no hidden human ingredients. 
Motives:
During an earlier trade she sold a breeding portion while knowing its final maintenance interval was shorter than the buyer expected. She described the stock accurately in other respects and omitted that inconvenient result. The buyer lost the brood and demanded compensation. Zhao repaid the stock price, not the spent medicines, and still argues privately that the handling contributed. Her observation slips and the buyer’s feeding times establish the omission. Du knows the dispute exists but has not seen both sets of records. She dislikes remembering how she made someone else bear a risk she understood.
characters.appearance: An intensely attractive adult woman with dark red-brown eyes, full lips and glossy black hair divided into two long braids threaded with small copper beads. A fitted charcoal inner robe lies beneath a flowing coral-red outer layer, with narrow cream bands at the wrists. Lacquered brood boxes hang from a dark silk belt; a faint branching cultivation scar follows one collarbone. She stands with a small closed brood box balanced on one palm while two fingers of the other hand rest attentively against its lacquered lid.
traits: Quirk: She listens to a closed brood box before deciding whether to sit down for supper.
Wants / Fears: She seeks independent feed and fears becoming the sort of teacher who creates dependence.
Pattern: She attends carefully to the brood but can overlook people while a cycle troubles her.
Bond: Du Wenzhi is a respected trading contemporary; Jin Lushu questions the uses of supplied material.
abilities: Scarlet Hearth Reinforcement — a prepared internal Gu cycle supports her actual Body attainment, consuming reserves and risking specific backlash if disrupted.
Identified Brood Handling — learned care of finite real stock; release requires preparation, a reachable target and a susceptible host.

characters.name: Wu Sen
characters.cultivation: Qi Path — Middle Spirit Transformation. Alchemical expertise and his demonic Marrow-to-Jade preparation are learned arts, not separate Body or Martial attainment.
characters.summary: Wu Sen learned alchemy in a small household whose furnace was worth more than its dwelling.
characters.basicInfo:
Background:
Wu Sen learned alchemy in a small household whose furnace was worth more than its dwelling. He still remembers the pleasure of his first patient standing without help. Advancement brought better furnaces, rarer ingredients and an inherited preparation whose effectiveness rested on cultivated human marrow. He examined the process, understood what it required and chose to keep using it. 
He travels between refining cities with a portable furnace core, trading legitimate medicines and reserving particular batches for trusted buyers.
